docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Post-hoc scorecard toolkit

Evaluation for saved agent runs

Ingest a dump or trace, score 47 metrics, and read an eight-question trustworthiness card. Library, CLI, and optional Streamlit UI. Does not execute your agent or act as a live safety control.

Get started Metric catalog GitHub Python ≥ 3.12 Apache 2.0 47 metrics Before you upload traces. Do not send personal, confidential, or regulated data to a hosted judge without authorization. Privacy and data

docs.title: bundle
docs.text:
Export one fully-scored run as a single portable, versioned JSON bundle.

Today a scored run only exists as whatever is currently in a Streamlit session or a caller's own variables; there is no way to save a complete run (the sealed record, its trace, every metric's result, and the eight-question profile) to reopen, share, or diff later. This is the useful core of an older, parked design's "portable zip bundle" idea (feature/portable-eval-kernel, dormant, shares only the repo's root commit with this branch), kept narrow on purpose: a flat JSON export of what ingest_any / score_metrics / build_profile already produce, not a new live-capture schema or a scheduler. A full live- harness Evidence Package stays roadmap, documented separately outside this codebase; aixeval.cli wraps this module as aixeval score|report|reband|replay.

build_run_bundle takes the three pieces of output a caller already has in hand after running the pipeline once: no new computation, no model calls, nothing re-derived. replay_bundle is the inverse check: given a saved bundle, confirm that re-scoring its own record reproduces exactly what was saved, with no model call either. compare_bundles is a different check again: given two independently-produced bundles, report whether their profiles diverge beyond a tolerance, software support for an independent-rerun safeguard, not a replacement for it.

build_run_bundle(result, scored, profile, *, judge=None)

Assemble one JSON-serializable bundle for a fully-scored run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default result IngestResult

The IngestResult from ingest_any (or ingest_inspect_eval's per-epoch results). spans, if present, are flattened to plain dicts; the bundle never holds live Span objects.

required scored list[dict[str, Any]]

score_metrics(result.record)'s return value: one row per metric, already graded.

required profile dict[str, Any]

build_profile(scored)'s return value: the eight-question card plus applied_hard_stops.

required judge str | None

Which judge model(s) produced the record's verdicts, e.g. "vllm · gemma-3-12b-it". Added as a judge key only when given, so bundles from callers that don't track it are unchanged.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

A flat dict safe to pass straight to json.dumps. Carries a schema_version so a future format change can be detected on read rather than silently misread.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def build_run_bundle(
    result: IngestResult,
    scored: list[dict[str, Any]],
    profile: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    judge: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble one JSON-serializable bundle for a fully-scored run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        The ``IngestResult`` from ``ingest_any`` (or ``ingest_inspect_eval``'s
        per-epoch results). ``spans``, if present, are flattened to plain
        dicts; the bundle never holds live ``Span`` objects.
    scored
        ``score_metrics(result.record)``'s return value: one row per
        metric, already graded.
    profile
        ``build_profile(scored)``'s return value: the eight-question
        card plus ``applied_hard_stops``.
    judge
        Which judge model(s) produced the record's verdicts, e.g.
        ``"vllm · gemma-3-12b-it"``. Added as a ``judge`` key only when
        given, so bundles from callers that don't track it are unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A flat dict safe to pass straight to ``json.dumps``. Carries a
        ``schema_version`` so a future format change can be detected on
        read rather than silently misread.
    """
    bundle: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema_version": BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "source_kind": result.source_kind,
        "record": result.record,
        "spans": [asdict(span) for span in result.spans] if result.spans is not None else None,
        "trajectory": result.trajectory,
        "contamination_evidence": result.contamination_evidence,
        "scored_results": scored,
        "profile": profile,
    }
    if judge is not None:
        bundle["judge"] = judge
    return bundle

write_run_bundle(bundle, path)

Write a bundle built by build_run_bundle to path as formatted JSON.

Creates parent directories if they do not exist, so --out runs/bundle.json does not require a prior mkdir.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def write_run_bundle(bundle: dict[str, Any], path: str | Path) -> None:
    """Write a bundle built by ``build_run_bundle`` to ``path`` as formatted JSON.

    Creates parent directories if they do not exist, so ``--out runs/bundle.json``
    does not require a prior ``mkdir``.
    """
    out = Path(path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(bundle, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

docs.title: replay_bundle
docs.text:
replay_bundle(bundle)

Re-score a bundle's own record and confirm it reproduces the saved results.

No model call: every scorer prefers a verdict already written on the record over computing a fresh one (the same discipline grounding, tool_call_accuracy, and every other judge-backed metric already use), so re-running score_metrics on the bundle's own record reproduces the same verdicts without calling a judge again. This is the offline-replay guarantee the Deliverable 2 design names as a Phase 0 exit criterion ("a golden Evidence Package replays bit-for- bit"), proven here for what this toolkit's own bundle format actually carries, not yet for a live harness's larger Evidence Package.

Returns:

Type Description dict

{"matches": bool, "metric_diffs": [...], "profile_diffs": [...]}. Both diff lists are empty on a clean replay. Each diff entry names what was saved and what replay actually produced, so a mismatch is diagnosable, not just a bare failure.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def replay_bundle(bundle: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Re-score a bundle's own record and confirm it reproduces the saved results.

    No model call: every scorer prefers a verdict already written on the
    record over computing a fresh one (the same discipline ``grounding``,
    ``tool_call_accuracy``, and every other judge-backed metric already
    use), so re-running ``score_metrics`` on the bundle's own ``record``
    reproduces the same verdicts without calling a judge again. This is
    the offline-replay guarantee the Deliverable 2 design names as a
    Phase 0 exit criterion ("a golden Evidence Package replays bit-for-
    bit"), proven here for what this toolkit's own bundle format
    actually carries, not yet for a live harness's larger Evidence
    Package.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{"matches": bool, "metric_diffs": [...], "profile_diffs": [...]}``.
        Both diff lists are empty on a clean replay. Each diff entry
        names what was saved and what replay actually produced, so a
        mismatch is diagnosable, not just a bare failure.
    """
    from aixeval.scorecard.metrics import score_metrics  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.scorecard.profile import build_profile  # noqa: PLC0415

    replayed_all = score_metrics(bundle["record"])
    saved_by_id = {row["metric_id"]: row for row in bundle["scored_results"]}
    replayed_by_id = {row["metric_id"]: row for row in replayed_all}
    # Bundles may store a selected subset (CLI ``--metrics`` / scenario.json).
    # Replay the saved ids only: extra catalog rows are not part of this card.
    metric_diffs = [
        {"metric_id": metric_id, "saved": saved_by_id.get(metric_id), "replayed": replayed_by_id.get(metric_id)}
        for metric_id in sorted(saved_by_id)
        if saved_by_id.get(metric_id) != replayed_by_id.get(metric_id)
    ]
    replayed_results = [replayed_by_id[metric_id] for metric_id in saved_by_id if metric_id in replayed_by_id]
    replayed_profile = build_profile(replayed_results)

    saved_profile = bundle["profile"]
    profile_diffs = [
        {"dimension": key, "saved": saved_profile.get(key), "replayed": replayed_profile.get(key)}
        for key in sorted(set(saved_profile) | set(replayed_profile))
        if not _profile_values_match(key, saved_profile.get(key), replayed_profile.get(key))
    ]

    return {
        "matches": not metric_diffs and not profile_diffs,
        "metric_diffs": metric_diffs,
        "profile_diffs": profile_diffs,
    }

docs.title: compare_bundles
docs.text:
compare_bundles(bundle_a, bundle_b, *, max_grade_drift=1)

Compare two independently-produced bundles of the same task.

An independent-rerun check: re-executing the same task separately and flagging a profile that diverges too far, not a strict bit-for-bit match, since decoding/judge non-determinism across a real re-run is expected. This toolkit has no bootstrapped confidence interval to compare against, so max_grade_drift (a plain band-count tolerance) is used in its place. This function does not re-execute anything itself; it only diffs two bundles a caller already produced, e.g. by running aixeval score twice (independently, or with live judges) on what is meant to be the same task.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default bundle_a dict[str, Any]

Two bundles from read_run_bundle/build_run_bundle, ideally scoring the same underlying task.

required bundle_b dict[str, Any]

Two bundles from read_run_bundle/build_run_bundle, ideally scoring the same underlying task.

required max_grade_drift int

How many grade bands apart two dimensions may be before being flagged as diverged. 1 (the default) tolerates the ordinary judge noise already documented for this toolkit's own judges (trajectory_optimality, pairwise_preference); 0 requires an exact grade match.

1

Returns:

Type Description dict

diverged (bool), and dimension_diffs: one entry per dimension that diverges. A dimension where both sides have a grade and they differ by more than max_grade_drift is flagged with drift set to that gap. A dimension that is N/A on one side and scored on the other is also flagged (drift is None): missing evidence vs a real grade is a difference, not a match. Both-N/A is skipped.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def compare_bundles(bundle_a: dict[str, Any], bundle_b: dict[str, Any], *, max_grade_drift: int = 1) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare two independently-produced bundles of the same task.

    An independent-rerun check: re-executing the same task separately
    and flagging a profile that diverges too far, not a strict
    bit-for-bit match, since decoding/judge non-determinism across a
    real re-run is expected. This toolkit has no bootstrapped
    confidence interval to compare against, so ``max_grade_drift``
    (a plain band-count tolerance) is used in its place. This function
    does not re-execute anything
    itself; it only diffs two bundles a caller already produced,
    e.g. by running ``aixeval score`` twice (independently, or
    with live judges) on what is meant to be the same task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    bundle_a, bundle_b
        Two bundles from ``read_run_bundle``/``build_run_bundle``,
        ideally scoring the same underlying task.
    max_grade_drift
        How many grade bands apart two dimensions may be before
        being flagged as diverged. 1 (the default) tolerates the
        ordinary judge noise already documented for this toolkit's
        own judges (``trajectory_optimality``, ``pairwise_preference``);
        0 requires an exact grade match.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``diverged`` (bool), and ``dimension_diffs``: one entry per
        dimension that diverges. A dimension where both sides have a
        grade and they differ by more than ``max_grade_drift`` is
        flagged with ``drift`` set to that gap. A dimension that is
        N/A on one side and scored on the other is also flagged
        (``drift`` is ``None``): missing evidence vs a real grade is
        a difference, not a match. Both-N/A is skipped.
    """
    profile_a, profile_b = bundle_a["profile"], bundle_b["profile"]
    dimension_diffs = []
    for dimension in sorted(set(profile_a) | set(profile_b)):
        if dimension == "applied_hard_stops":
            continue
        grade_a, grade_b = profile_a.get(dimension), profile_b.get(dimension)
        if grade_a is None and grade_b is None:
            continue
        if grade_a is None or grade_b is None:
            dimension_diffs.append({"dimension": dimension, "grade_a": grade_a, "grade_b": grade_b, "drift": None})
            continue
        drift = abs(grade_a - grade_b)
        if drift > max_grade_drift:
            dimension_diffs.append({"dimension": dimension, "grade_a": grade_a, "grade_b": grade_b, "drift": drift})
    return {"diverged": bool(dimension_diffs), "dimension_diffs": dimension_diffs}

Read back a bundle written by write_run_bundle.

Type Description ValueError

The file's schema_version is missing or doesn't match BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION: a newer or malformed bundle is rejected rather than silently misread.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def read_run_bundle(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read back a bundle written by ``write_run_bundle``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The file's ``schema_version`` is missing or doesn't match
        ``BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION``: a newer or malformed bundle is
        rejected rather than silently misread.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    bundle = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    version = bundle.get("schema_version")
    if version != BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        if _looks_like_ui_saved_run(bundle):
            msg = (
                f"{path} looks like a UI saved_run.json, not a run bundle. "
                "Score the scenario's trace and write a bundle first: "
                "aixeval score <folder>/trace.json --out run.json && aixeval report run.json"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        msg = f"unknown run-bundle schema_version {version!r}, expected {BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION!r}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return bundle

print_bundle_example()

Print a small round-tripped bundle: build, write, read back.

Source code in src/aixeval/bundle.py 
def print_bundle_example() -> None:
    """Print a small round-tripped bundle: build, write, read back."""
    from aixeval.ingest.pipeline import ingest_any  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.scorecard.metrics import score_metrics  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.scorecard.profile import build_profile  # noqa: PLC0415

    result = ingest_any({"expected": "Paris", "output": "Paris"})
    scored = score_metrics(result.record)
    profile = build_profile(scored)
    bundle = build_run_bundle(result, scored, profile)
    print(f"bundle keys: {sorted(bundle.keys())}")
    print(f"schema_version: {bundle['schema_version']}")
    print(f"capability grade: {bundle['profile']['capability']}")

    import tempfile  # noqa: PLC0415

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        path = Path(tmp) / "run.json"
        write_run_bundle(bundle, path)
        read_back = read_run_bundle(path)
        print(f"round-tripped, same record: {read_back['record'] == bundle['record']}")

        replay = replay_bundle(read_back)
        print(f"replay matches, no model call: {replay['matches']}")

docs.title: cli
docs.text:
A thin command-line entrypoint for scoring, reporting, and comparing saved runs.

Salvaged from the old feature/portable-eval-kernel vision's CLI idea (run/validate/reband/rescore/rerun), kept narrow on purpose, same as bundle.py and reband.py: commands wrapping the library calls that already exist (ingest_any/score_metrics/ build_profile, plus build_run_bundle/reband_profile/ replay_bundle/compare_bundles/score_cross_run_consistency), not a new scheduler or a new execution model. No new dependency: stdlib argparse.

aixeval score  <dump.json> [--declared-fields FIELDS.json] \
    [--overlay OVERLAY.json] [--metrics id,id] \
    [--live-judges grounding,refusal] [--audit-contamination] \
    [--test-retest-metric grounding --test-retest-n 3] [--out run.json]
aixeval report <run.json>
aixeval reband <run.json> [--cutoffs 0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8] \
    [--hard-stop unsafe_action_cap=0.15]
aixeval replay <run.json>
aixeval compare <run_a.json> <run_b.json> [--max-grade-drift 1]
aixeval cross-run-consistency <suite_dir> --metric grounding \
    [--bootstrap-samples 2000] [--seed 0]

compare is software support for an independent-rerun safeguard: it diffs two already-produced bundles, it does not re-execute anything. See aixeval.bundle.compare_bundles for exactly what it proves and what it doesn't.

cross-run-consistency is the same non-reexecuting philosophy one level up: <suite_dir> holds one subdirectory per problem, each holding two or more already-produced run bundles of that same problem (e.g. from running aixeval score --live-judges ... --out several times). This command reads them, groups them by subdirectory name, and reports one variance band for the whole set -- it does not call a judge or re-execute anything either. See aixeval.cross_run_consistency for what the band means and how "unstable" is decided.

Parse arguments and dispatch to the selected subcommand.

Returns the process exit code: 0 on success, 1 on a handled error (bad input, missing file). Never lets a user-facing input mistake surface as a raw Python traceback.

Source code in src/aixeval/cli.py 
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse arguments and dispatch to the selected subcommand.

    Returns the process exit code: 0 on success, 1 on a handled error
    (bad input, missing file). Never lets a user-facing input mistake
    surface as a raw Python traceback.
    """
    parser = _build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return _COMMANDS[args.command](args)
    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

docs.title: cross_run_consistency
docs.text:
Cross-run consistency: one variance band across a whole test set of problems.

This toolkit scores one record at a time (score_metrics(record) -> ...) and has no concept anywhere else of a "test set" -- many problems, each run more than once. consistency and test_retest_stability both grade variance within a single record (a two-run spread, or variance across reruns of one unchanged input). Neither aggregates across many problems. This module is the first piece of that missing layer: given many problems, each with several independently-produced run bundles of the same task, it computes one variance figure and one band for the whole set -- what a harness actually needs to report, rather than one number per problem.

Deliberately NOT a POSTHOC_METRICS entry: it doesn't fit the score_x(record) -> result shape every scorer in scorecard/ uses, the same reason reband/replay/compare live at this top level instead of under scorecard/. A caller already has the bundles (e.g. from running aixeval score on the same task several times); this module does not run anything itself.

Grading reuses the exact C(0.10) budget and banding test_retest_stability already uses for a single record's rerun variance, applied here to the mean of many records' variances instead -- the same construct, one level up.

"Unstable" is a declared policy, not pinned anywhere upstream: a problem counts as unstable if its runs did not all land on the exact same raw score (variance > 0), the simplest reading of "gave different results across runs." Flagged here, not hidden, same discipline every other undocumented threshold in this toolkit gets.

docs.title: ProblemRuns dataclass
docs.text:
One problem's repeated-run bundles: the unit this module scores.

bundles must be at least two independently-produced run bundles (aixeval.bundle.build_run_bundle / read_run_bundle) of the same task -- e.g. aixeval score run several times on one problem, with live judges, so non-determinism actually has a chance to show up. Fewer than two usable bundles excludes the problem from the aggregate; it is not silently dropped.

Source code in src/aixeval/cross_run_consistency.py 
@dataclass
class ProblemRuns:
    """One problem's repeated-run bundles: the unit this module scores.

    ``bundles`` must be at least two independently-produced run
    bundles (``aixeval.bundle.build_run_bundle`` / ``read_run_bundle``)
    of the *same* task -- e.g. ``aixeval score`` run several times on
    one problem, with live judges, so non-determinism actually has a
    chance to show up. Fewer than two usable bundles excludes the
    problem from the aggregate; it is not silently dropped.
    """

    problem_id: str
    bundles: list[dict[str, Any]]

docs.title: score_cross_run_consistency
docs.text:
score_cross_run_consistency(
    problems,
    *,
    metric_id,
    bootstrap_samples=DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_SAMPLES,
    seed=None,
)

Score one metric's run-to-run variance across a whole set of problems.

For each problem, reads metric_id's raw_score from every bundle where that metric actually scored (N/A rows are skipped, same as a missing run). A problem with fewer than MIN_RUNS_PER_PROBLEM usable scores is excluded from the aggregate, listed in excluded_problems with why, never silently folded in as if it were stable.

The aggregate raw score is clamp(mean(per-problem variance) / 0.10, 0, 1), graded lower-is-better against the shared cutoff table -- the same C(0.10) construct test_retest_stability uses for one record, averaged here across many.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default problems list[ProblemRuns]

One ProblemRuns per problem in the set.

required metric_id str

Which metric's raw_score to read from each bundle's scored_results. Any metric id works; this module does not care which one, same as compare_bundles not caring which dimension it is diffing.

required bootstrap_samples int

How many resamples the percentile bootstrap draws. Only used when at least 2 problems scored; a smaller set still returns a (wider, noisier) interval rather than refusing to compute one.

DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_SAMPLES seed int | None

Seeds the bootstrap's random resampling for a reproducible interval across repeated calls on the same input. None (the default) draws a fresh interval each call.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

status ("scored" or "na"). When scored: raw_score (the clamped ratio used for grading), mean_variance (the unclamped mean, for transparency), grade, problems_scored, unstable_share (fraction of scored problems with variance > 0), unstable_problems (those problems' own id/variance/runs, the "only need to check those" list), per_problem (every scored problem's own id/variance/runs), bootstrap_ci ((low, high) over the per-problem variances, or None if fewer than 2 problems scored), and excluded_problems (problem id, reason, and how many usable runs were actually found). When no problem has enough usable runs: na_reason plus the same excluded_problems list, so the caller can see why.

Source code in src/aixeval/cross_run_consistency.py 
def score_cross_run_consistency(
    problems: list[ProblemRuns],
    *,
    metric_id: str,
    bootstrap_samples: int = DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_SAMPLES,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score one metric's run-to-run variance across a whole set of problems.

    For each problem, reads ``metric_id``'s ``raw_score`` from every
    bundle where that metric actually scored (N/A rows are skipped,
    same as a missing run). A problem with fewer than
    ``MIN_RUNS_PER_PROBLEM`` usable scores is excluded from the
    aggregate, listed in ``excluded_problems`` with why, never
    silently folded in as if it were stable.

    The aggregate raw score is ``clamp(mean(per-problem variance) /
    0.10, 0, 1)``, graded lower-is-better against the shared cutoff
    table -- the same ``C(0.10)`` construct ``test_retest_stability``
    uses for one record, averaged here across many.

    Parameters
    ----------
    problems
        One ``ProblemRuns`` per problem in the set.
    metric_id
        Which metric's ``raw_score`` to read from each bundle's
        ``scored_results``. Any metric id works; this module does not
        care which one, same as ``compare_bundles`` not caring which
        dimension it is diffing.
    bootstrap_samples
        How many resamples the percentile bootstrap draws. Only used
        when at least 2 problems scored; a smaller set still returns
        a (wider, noisier) interval rather than refusing to compute
        one.
    seed
        Seeds the bootstrap's random resampling for a reproducible
        interval across repeated calls on the same input. ``None``
        (the default) draws a fresh interval each call.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"na"``). When scored:
        ``raw_score`` (the clamped ratio used for grading),
        ``mean_variance`` (the unclamped mean, for transparency),
        ``grade``, ``problems_scored``, ``unstable_share`` (fraction
        of scored problems with ``variance > 0``), ``unstable_problems``
        (those problems' own id/variance/runs, the "only need to check
        those" list), ``per_problem`` (every scored problem's own
        id/variance/runs), ``bootstrap_ci`` (``(low, high)`` over the
        per-problem variances, or ``None`` if fewer than 2 problems
        scored), and ``excluded_problems`` (problem id, reason, and
        how many usable runs were actually found).
        When no problem has enough usable runs: ``na_reason`` plus the
        same ``excluded_problems`` list, so the caller can see why.
    """
    scored_problems: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    excluded: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for problem in problems:
        scores = _usable_scores(problem, metric_id)
        if len(scores) < MIN_RUNS_PER_PROBLEM:
            excluded.append(
                {
                    "problem_id": problem.problem_id,
                    "reason": "missing_evidence",
                    "runs_available": len(scores),
                }
            )
            continue
        variance = statistics.pvariance(scores)
        scored_problems.append(
            {
                "problem_id": problem.problem_id,
                "variance": variance,
                "runs": len(scores),
                "unstable": variance > UNSTABLE_VARIANCE_EPSILON,
            }
        )

    if not scored_problems:
        return {
            "status": "na",
            "na_reason": "missing_evidence",
            "excluded_problems": excluded,
        }

    variances = [problem["variance"] for problem in scored_problems]
    mean_variance = statistics.fmean(variances)
    raw_score = min(1.0, mean_variance / VARIANCE_BUDGET)
    grade = grade_for_raw_score(raw_score, higher_is_better=False)

    unstable_problems = [problem for problem in scored_problems if problem["unstable"]]
    unstable_share = len(unstable_problems) / len(scored_problems)
    bootstrap_ci = _bootstrap_ci(variances, samples=bootstrap_samples, seed=seed)

    return {
        "status": "scored",
        "raw_score": raw_score,
        "mean_variance": mean_variance,
        "grade": grade,
        "problems_scored": len(scored_problems),
        "unstable_share": unstable_share,
        "unstable_problems": unstable_problems,
        "per_problem": scored_problems,
        "bootstrap_ci": bootstrap_ci,
        "excluded_problems": excluded,
    }

audit_expected_in_inputs(
    record, input_texts, *, enabled=False
)

If gold overlaps enough of any single input text, mark leak and cancel.

Off by default. Does not open files. Does not call a model. A hit sets contaminated, cancelled, and evidence_status="cancelled" on the returned record: every scorer then reports N/A uniformly, which on its own gives no way to tell why. The second return value is that why: a human-readable explanation of the overlap fraction and which input text it matched (truncated), kept out of the record itself rather than added as a new field, the same reason a live judge's rationale is returned alongside the record instead of written into it. None when there was no hit, or the audit never ran (off, no expected, gold too short).

Returns:

Type Description tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]

The (possibly cancelled) record, and the evidence string or None.

def audit_expected_in_inputs(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    input_texts: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    enabled: bool = False,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]:
    """If gold overlaps enough of any single input text, mark leak and cancel.

    Off by default. Does not open files. Does not call a model.
    A hit sets ``contaminated``, ``cancelled``, and
    ``evidence_status="cancelled"`` on the returned record: every
    scorer then reports N/A uniformly, which on its own gives no way to
    tell *why*. The second return value is that why: a human-readable
    explanation of the overlap fraction and which input text it matched
    (truncated), kept out of the record itself rather than added as a
    new field, the same reason a live judge's rationale is returned
    alongside the record instead of written into it. ``None`` when
    there was no hit, or the audit never ran (off, no ``expected``,
    gold too short).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]
        The (possibly cancelled) record, and the evidence string or
        ``None``.
    """
    out = dict(record)
    if not enabled:
        return validate_record(out), None

    expected = record.get("expected")
    if not isinstance(expected, str):
        return validate_record(out), None
    needle = expected.strip().casefold()
    if len(needle) < MIN_EXPECTED_LEN:
        return validate_record(out), None

    windows = _windows(needle, WINDOW_WORDS)
    for raw in input_texts:
        if not isinstance(raw, str):
            continue
        haystack = raw.strip().casefold()
        fraction = _overlap_fraction(windows, haystack)
        if fraction >= OVERLAP_THRESHOLD:
            out["contaminated"] = True
            out["cancelled"] = True
            out["evidence_status"] = "cancelled"
            return validate_record(out), _evidence(fraction, raw)
    return validate_record(out), None

def ingest_suite(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Load many simple JSON objects (array or ``.jsonl``) into sealed records.

    Each row uses the same copy rules as ``ingest_dump``. One bad row fails
    the whole file.
    """
    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for index, payload in enumerate(load_json_suite(path)):
        try:
            records.append(validate_record(simple_record_fields(payload)))
        except ValueError as exc:
            msg = f"suite item {index}: {exc}"
            raise ValueError(msg) from exc
    return records

def collect_langfuse_input_texts(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Strings an audit may search: root ``input`` and each observation ``input``.

    A dict or list is JSON-encoded so a gold phrase inside structured
    input can still match. ``output`` fields are not collected.
    """
    texts: list[str] = []
    _append_input_text(texts, payload.get("input"))
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if isinstance(observations, list):
        for item in observations:
            if isinstance(item, dict):
                _append_input_text(texts, item.get("input"))
    return texts

    *,
    declared_fields=None,
    overlay=None,
    audit_contamination=False,

Ingest one dump, whatever its shape, and merge in any user-declared fields.

Tries the multi-agent trace parsers first (detect_and_parse: Langfuse/OTel/Patronus). If the payload doesn't match any of those shapes, falls back to the simple single-record dump path.

For a Langfuse-shaped trace, also runs the existing ingest_langfuse field rules (expected from metadata, stated_confidence, latency_sec, last-generation output) on top of the trace; that extraction only exists for Langfuse's shape, so an OTel or Patronus trace only gets the generic fallback below (output = last span with a non-empty output, steps = span count). This asymmetry is real, not an oversight: no one has written an equivalent metadata-reading bridge for the other two formats yet.

overlay, if given, is passed to build_overlay_fields along with the parsed spans: gold roles, fault-containment verdicts, the stall flag, and MAS unsafe-step counts for the four multi-agent metrics (delegation_accuracy, error_propagation_containment, deadlock_livelock, cumulative_unsafe_action_mas). Unlike declared_fields, this isn't a flat field dict: faults_total and (when every fault has a containment verdict) faults_contained are derived by cross-referencing the overlay's annotations against faults/delegations actually found in the trace, not typed directly. Only meaningful for a trace; raises if given alongside a payload that isn't one.

declared_fields are gold/annotation fields the caller supplies directly (expected answer, should_refuse, budgets, and so on). These always win over anything auto-derived from the trace, dump, or overlay, since the user is asserting ground truth, not a guess.

audit_contamination, only meaningful for a trace, runs audit_expected_in_inputs against every span's own input text (collect_trace_input_texts) once expected is on the record. Off by default, same as the audit function's own default. Skipped entirely when declared_fields already asserts contaminated explicitly: a human's declared ground truth always wins over the automated check, never the other way round. A hit's explanation (overlap fraction, matched input text) comes back on IngestResult.contamination_evidence, not as a new record field; the record itself gets cancelled, which makes every scorer report N/A uniformly and would otherwise erase why.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

validate_record rejects an unknown or mistyped field name (from the dump, overlay, or declared_fields); or overlay is given but payload isn't a multi-agent trace.

def ingest_any(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    declared_fields: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    overlay: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    audit_contamination: bool = False,
) -> IngestResult:
    """Ingest one dump, whatever its shape, and merge in any user-declared fields.

    Tries the multi-agent trace parsers first (``detect_and_parse``:
    Langfuse/OTel/Patronus). If the payload doesn't match any of those
    shapes, falls back to the simple single-record dump path.

    For a Langfuse-shaped trace, also runs the existing
    ``ingest_langfuse`` field rules (``expected`` from ``metadata``,
    ``stated_confidence``, ``latency_sec``, last-generation ``output``)
    on top of the trace; that extraction only exists for Langfuse's
    shape, so an OTel or Patronus trace only gets the generic fallback
    below (``output`` = last span with a non-empty output, ``steps`` =
    span count). This asymmetry is real, not an oversight: no one has
    written an equivalent metadata-reading bridge for the other two
    formats yet.

    ``overlay``, if given, is passed to ``build_overlay_fields`` along
    with the parsed spans: gold roles, fault-containment verdicts,
    the stall flag, and MAS unsafe-step counts for the four multi-agent
    metrics (``delegation_accuracy``, ``error_propagation_containment``,
    ``deadlock_livelock``, ``cumulative_unsafe_action_mas``). Unlike
    ``declared_fields``, this isn't a flat field dict: ``faults_total``
    and (when every fault has a containment verdict) ``faults_contained``
    are derived by cross-referencing the overlay's annotations against
    faults/delegations actually found in the trace, not typed directly.
    Only meaningful for a trace; raises if given alongside a payload
    that isn't one.

    ``declared_fields`` are gold/annotation fields the caller supplies
    directly (expected answer, ``should_refuse``, budgets, and so on).
    These always win over anything auto-derived from the trace, dump,
    or overlay, since the user is asserting ground truth, not a guess.

    ``audit_contamination``, only meaningful for a trace, runs
    ``audit_expected_in_inputs`` against every span's own ``input``
    text (``collect_trace_input_texts``) once ``expected`` is on the
    record. Off by default, same as the audit function's own default.
    Skipped entirely when ``declared_fields`` already asserts
    ``contaminated`` explicitly: a human's declared ground truth
    always wins over the automated check, never the other way round.
    A hit's explanation (overlap fraction, matched input text) comes
    back on ``IngestResult.contamination_evidence``, not as a new
    record field; the record itself gets ``cancelled``, which makes
    every scorer report N/A uniformly and would otherwise erase why.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``validate_record`` rejects an unknown or mistyped field name
        (from the dump, ``overlay``, or ``declared_fields``); or
        ``overlay`` is given but ``payload`` isn't a multi-agent trace.
    """
    try:
        spans = detect_and_parse(payload)
    except ValueError:
        if overlay is not None:
            msg = "overlay requires a multi-agent trace; this payload parsed as a simple (non-trace) dump"
            raise ValueError(msg) from None
        base = simple_record_fields(payload)
        record = validate_record({**base, **(declared_fields or {})})
        return IngestResult(record=record, spans=None, trajectory=None, source_kind="simple_dump")

    base = (
        langfuse_record_fields(payload)
        if isinstance(payload.get("observations"), list)
        else _trace_fallback_fields(spans)
    )
    overlay_fields = build_overlay_fields(spans, overlay) if overlay is not None else {}
    merged = {**base, **overlay_fields, **(declared_fields or {})}
    contamination_evidence = None
    if audit_contamination and "contaminated" not in (declared_fields or {}):
        merged, contamination_evidence = audit_expected_in_inputs(
            merged, collect_trace_input_texts(spans), enabled=True
        )
    record = validate_record(merged)
    return IngestResult(
        record=record,
        spans=spans,
        trajectory=format_trajectory(spans),
        source_kind="trace",
        contamination_evidence=contamination_evidence,
    )

def validate_record(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Check names and types. Unknown keys and bad types raise ``ValueError``.

    Absence is legal. This does not check that a translator mapped the
    right source field.
    """
    unknown = sorted(set(record) - set(RECORD_FIELDS))
    if unknown:
        shown = ", ".join(unknown)
        msg = f"Unknown sealed-record field(s): {shown}"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    checked: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in record.items():
        checked[key] = _check_field(key, value)
    return checked

docs.title: audit
docs.text:
Audit after ingest: gold overlapping declared input texts cancels the case.

Matching is windowed-n-gram overlap, not a single exact-substring check: the standard technique the data-contamination-detection literature uses (GPT-3/GPT-4's own leak screens are both variants of this), chosen over embeddings or an LLM judge deliberately: it stays free and deterministic, at the cost of still missing a true paraphrase (same ceiling the field's own methods have, not a gap unique to this implementation). For gold text at or under WINDOW_WORDS words, this is exactly a full-string containment check (one window, the whole text); it degrades to the prior exact-match behavior for a short gold answer, and only starts catching a partial leak (one word changed, reformatted, mid-leak cut) once gold is longer than one window.

def ingest_suite(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Load many simple JSON objects (array or ``.jsonl``) into sealed records.

    Each row uses the same copy rules as ``ingest_dump``. One bad row fails
    the whole file.

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    return records

def simple_record_fields(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Copy sealed-record keys. Expand a letter ``output`` when ``choices`` exist.

    Public (not a leading-underscore helper): also reused directly by
    ``aixeval.ingest.pipeline.ingest_any`` for its simple-dump
    fallback path, so the one copy-known-fields rule lives in one place.
    """
    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key in RECORD_FIELDS:
        if key in payload and payload[key] is not None:
            record[key] = payload[key]

    choices = payload.get("choices")
    output = record.get("output")
    if isinstance(choices, dict) and isinstance(output, str):
        expanded = _expand_letter(output, choices)
        if expanded is not None:
            record["output"] = expanded
    return record

def collect_langfuse_input_texts(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Strings an audit may search: root ``input`` and each observation ``input``.

    A dict or list is JSON-encoded so a gold phrase inside structured
    input can still match. ``output`` fields are not collected.
    """
    texts: list[str] = []

    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if isinstance(observations, list):

            if isinstance(item, dict):

    return texts

Source code in src/aixeval/ingest/langfuse.py 
def langfuse_record_fields(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Public: also reused by ``ingest.pipeline.ingest_any`` for Langfuse payloads."""
    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
    metadata = payload.get("metadata")
    meta = metadata if isinstance(metadata, dict) else {}

    expected = _optional_str(payload.get("expected")) or _optional_str(meta.get("expected"))
    if expected is not None:
        record["expected"] = expected

    output = _optional_str(payload.get("output"))
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    obs_list = observations if isinstance(observations, list) else []
    if output is None:
        output = _last_generation_output(obs_list)
    if output is not None:
        record["output"] = output

    confidence = meta.get("stated_confidence")
    if confidence is not None:
        record["stated_confidence"] = confidence

    latency = payload.get("latency")
    if latency is not None:
        record["latency_sec"] = latency

    if obs_list:
        record["steps"] = len(obs_list)
    return record

def load_json_suite(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Read many objects: ``.jsonl`` (one object per line) or a JSON array."""
    file_path = Path(path)
    text = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if file_path.suffix.lower() == ".jsonl":
        return _load_jsonl(text)
    payload = json.loads(text)
    if not isinstance(payload, list):
        msg = "ingest_suite accepts a JSON array or a .jsonl file"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for index, item in enumerate(payload):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            msg = f"suite item {index} must be a JSON object"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        rows.append(item)
    return rows

Declared overlay for a multi-agent run: ground truth no trace contains.

An overlay is a separate annotation, written by the harness or a person, keyed to one run. build_overlay_fields combines it with the spans derived from the trace and returns flat record fields for the metrics.

A field is left out when its evidence is incomplete, so the metric reports N/A instead of scoring a guess.

def validate_overlay(overlay: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Check the overlay's shape and types. Unknown top-level keys are rejected."""
    allowed = {"faults", "gold_roles", "run_stalled", "mas_unsafe_steps", "mas_total_steps"}
    unknown = sorted(set(overlay) - allowed)
    if unknown:
        msg = f"unknown overlay key(s): {', '.join(unknown)}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    for item in _list(overlay, "faults"):
        if not isinstance(item.get("span_id"), str) or not isinstance(item.get("contained"), bool):
            msg = "each fault needs a string span_id and a bool contained"
            raise ValueError(msg)
    for item in _list(overlay, "gold_roles"):
        if not isinstance(item.get("subtask"), str) or not isinstance(item.get("agent"), str):
            msg = "each gold role needs a string subtask and a string agent"
            raise ValueError(msg)
    if "run_stalled" in overlay and not isinstance(overlay["run_stalled"], bool):
        msg = "run_stalled must be a bool"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    for key in ("mas_unsafe_steps", "mas_total_steps"):
        value = overlay.get(key)
        if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0):
            msg = f"{key} must be an int >= 0"
            raise ValueError(msg)

Incomplete evidence is omitted, so the metric reports N/A.

Source code in src/aixeval/ingest/overlay.py 
def build_overlay_fields(spans: list[Span], overlay: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return flat record fields from the trace and overlay.

    Incomplete evidence is omitted, so the metric reports N/A.
    """
    validate_overlay(overlay)
    fields: dict[str, Any] = {}

    faults = derive_faults(spans)
    fields["faults_total"] = len(faults)
    contained_by_span = {item["span_id"]: item["contained"] for item in _list(overlay, "faults")}
    if all(f["span_id"] in contained_by_span for f in faults):
        fields["faults_contained"] = sum(contained_by_span[f["span_id"]] for f in faults)

    gold_roles = _list(overlay, "gold_roles")
    fields["subtasks_total"] = len(gold_roles)
    delegations = derive_delegations(spans)
    if gold_roles and all(d["text"] is not None for d in delegations):
        correct = sum(
            1
            for role in gold_roles
            if any(d["text"] == role["subtask"] and d["recipient"] == role["agent"] for d in delegations)
        )
        fields["subtasks_correct"] = correct

    if "run_stalled" in overlay:
        fields["run_stalled"] = overlay["run_stalled"]
    for key in ("mas_unsafe_steps", "mas_total_steps"):
        if overlay.get(key) is not None:
            fields[key] = overlay[key]
    return fields

docs.text:
One entrypoint for any supported dump shape: detect, parse, bridge to a record.

The multi-agent trace parsers (Langfuse/OTel/Patronus, ingest.trace) and the simple single-record dump path (ingest.dumps) produce two different shapes: a Span list versus a flat sealed-record dict. Most metrics need declared fields (gold answer, budgets, safety flags) that no raw trace or dump carries on its own. This module bridges both paths into one call a UI makes once, and is explicit about what it can and cannot auto-derive: it never guesses a gold field.

@dataclass
class IngestResult:
    """One ingested run: a scoreable record, plus the raw trace if it was one.

    ``spans``/``trajectory`` are ``None`` for a simple (non-trace) dump:
    there is no step-by-step trail to show a judge or a MAS metric.
    ``contamination_evidence`` is ``None`` unless ``audit_contamination``
    found a hit, kept off the sealed record itself, same reason a live
    judge's rationale isn't written into the record either.
    """

    record: dict[str, Any]
    spans: list[Span] | None
    trajectory: str | None
    source_kind: str  # "trace" or "simple_dump"
    contamination_evidence: str | None = None

docs.text:
ingest_any(
    payload,
    *,
    declared_fields=None,
    overlay=None,
    audit_contamination=False,
)

Ingest one dump, whatever its shape, and merge in any user-declared fields.

Tries the multi-agent trace parsers first (detect_and_parse: Langfuse/OTel/Patronus). If the payload doesn't match any of those shapes, falls back to the simple single-record dump path.

For a Langfuse-shaped trace, also runs the existing ingest_langfuse field rules (expected from metadata, stated_confidence, latency_sec, last-generation output) on top of the trace; that extraction only exists for Langfuse's shape, so an OTel or Patronus trace only gets the generic fallback below (output = last span with a non-empty output, steps = span count). This asymmetry is real, not an oversight: no one has written an equivalent metadata-reading bridge for the other two formats yet.

overlay, if given, is passed to build_overlay_fields along with the parsed spans: gold roles, fault-containment verdicts, the stall flag, and MAS unsafe-step counts for the four multi-agent metrics (delegation_accuracy, error_propagation_containment, deadlock_livelock, cumulative_unsafe_action_mas). Unlike declared_fields, this isn't a flat field dict: faults_total and (when every fault has a containment verdict) faults_contained are derived by cross-referencing the overlay's annotations against faults/delegations actually found in the trace, not typed directly. Only meaningful for a trace; raises if given alongside a payload that isn't one.

declared_fields are gold/annotation fields the caller supplies directly (expected answer, should_refuse, budgets, and so on). These always win over anything auto-derived from the trace, dump, or overlay, since the user is asserting ground truth, not a guess.

audit_contamination, only meaningful for a trace, runs audit_expected_in_inputs against every span's own input text (collect_trace_input_texts) once expected is on the record. Off by default, same as the audit function's own default. Skipped entirely when declared_fields already asserts contaminated explicitly: a human's declared ground truth always wins over the automated check, never the other way round. A hit's explanation (overlap fraction, matched input text) comes back on IngestResult.contamination_evidence, not as a new record field; the record itself gets cancelled, which makes every scorer report N/A uniformly and would otherwise erase why.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

validate_record rejects an unknown or mistyped field name (from the dump, overlay, or declared_fields); or overlay is given but payload isn't a multi-agent trace.

Source code in src/aixeval/ingest/pipeline.py 
def ingest_any(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    declared_fields: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    overlay: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    audit_contamination: bool = False,
) -> IngestResult:
    """Ingest one dump, whatever its shape, and merge in any user-declared fields.

    Tries the multi-agent trace parsers first (``detect_and_parse``:
    Langfuse/OTel/Patronus). If the payload doesn't match any of those
    shapes, falls back to the simple single-record dump path.

    For a Langfuse-shaped trace, also runs the existing
    ``ingest_langfuse`` field rules (``expected`` from ``metadata``,
    ``stated_confidence``, ``latency_sec``, last-generation ``output``)
    on top of the trace; that extraction only exists for Langfuse's
    shape, so an OTel or Patronus trace only gets the generic fallback
    below (``output`` = last span with a non-empty output, ``steps`` =
    span count). This asymmetry is real, not an oversight: no one has
    written an equivalent metadata-reading bridge for the other two
    formats yet.

    ``overlay``, if given, is passed to ``build_overlay_fields`` along
    with the parsed spans: gold roles, fault-containment verdicts,
    the stall flag, and MAS unsafe-step counts for the four multi-agent
    metrics (``delegation_accuracy``, ``error_propagation_containment``,
    ``deadlock_livelock``, ``cumulative_unsafe_action_mas``). Unlike
    ``declared_fields``, this isn't a flat field dict: ``faults_total``
    and (when every fault has a containment verdict) ``faults_contained``
    are derived by cross-referencing the overlay's annotations against
    faults/delegations actually found in the trace, not typed directly.
    Only meaningful for a trace; raises if given alongside a payload
    that isn't one.

    ``declared_fields`` are gold/annotation fields the caller supplies
    directly (expected answer, ``should_refuse``, budgets, and so on).
    These always win over anything auto-derived from the trace, dump,
    or overlay, since the user is asserting ground truth, not a guess.

    ``audit_contamination``, only meaningful for a trace, runs
    ``audit_expected_in_inputs`` against every span's own ``input``
    text (``collect_trace_input_texts``) once ``expected`` is on the
    record. Off by default, same as the audit function's own default.
    Skipped entirely when ``declared_fields`` already asserts
    ``contaminated`` explicitly: a human's declared ground truth
    always wins over the automated check, never the other way round.
    A hit's explanation (overlap fraction, matched input text) comes
    back on ``IngestResult.contamination_evidence``, not as a new
    record field; the record itself gets ``cancelled``, which makes
    every scorer report N/A uniformly and would otherwise erase why.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``validate_record`` rejects an unknown or mistyped field name
        (from the dump, ``overlay``, or ``declared_fields``); or
        ``overlay`` is given but ``payload`` isn't a multi-agent trace.
    """
    try:
        spans = detect_and_parse(payload)
    except ValueError:
        if overlay is not None:
            msg = "overlay requires a multi-agent trace; this payload parsed as a simple (non-trace) dump"
            raise ValueError(msg) from None
        base = simple_record_fields(payload)
        record = validate_record({**base, **(declared_fields or {})})
        return IngestResult(record=record, spans=None, trajectory=None, source_kind="simple_dump")

    base = (
        langfuse_record_fields(payload)
        if isinstance(payload.get("observations"), list)
        else _trace_fallback_fields(spans)
    )
    overlay_fields = build_overlay_fields(spans, overlay) if overlay is not None else {}
    merged = {**base, **overlay_fields, **(declared_fields or {})}
    contamination_evidence = None
    if audit_contamination and "contaminated" not in (declared_fields or {}):
        merged, contamination_evidence = audit_expected_in_inputs(
            merged, collect_trace_input_texts(spans), enabled=True
        )
    record = validate_record(merged)
    return IngestResult(
        record=record,
        spans=spans,
        trajectory=format_trajectory(spans),
        source_kind="trace",
        contamination_evidence=contamination_evidence,
    )

ingest_inspect_eval(data, *, declared_fields=None)

Ingest an Inspect AI .eval file: one IngestResult per sample/epoch.

Unlike ingest_any, this doesn't take a parsed JSON dict: a .eval file is a Zstd-compressed zip archive, not plain JSON (see ingest.trace_inspect). Each sample/epoch pair in the file becomes its own result: each is a genuinely separate agent run on the same task, not something to merge into one record.

declared_fields, when given, is applied identically to every resulting record (same caller-always-wins discipline as ingest_any); there's no per-epoch override here.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

The archive doesn't parse (read_inspect_eval), a sample has no messages list (parse_inspect_sample), or validate_record rejects a field name (from the sample or declared_fields).

def ingest_inspect_eval(data: bytes, *, declared_fields: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[IngestResult]:
    """Ingest an Inspect AI ``.eval`` file: one ``IngestResult`` per sample/epoch.

    Unlike ``ingest_any``, this doesn't take a parsed JSON dict: a
    ``.eval`` file is a Zstd-compressed zip archive, not plain JSON (see
    ``ingest.trace_inspect``). Each sample/epoch pair in the file becomes
    its own result: each is a genuinely separate agent run on the same
    task, not something to merge into one record.

    ``declared_fields``, when given, is applied identically to every
    resulting record (same caller-always-wins discipline as
    ``ingest_any``); there's no per-epoch override here.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The archive doesn't parse (``read_inspect_eval``), a sample has
        no ``messages`` list (``parse_inspect_sample``), or
        ``validate_record`` rejects a field name (from the sample or
        ``declared_fields``).
    """
    results = []
    for sample in read_inspect_eval(data):
        spans = parse_inspect_sample(sample)
        base = _trace_fallback_fields(spans)
        target = sample.get("target")
        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
            base["expected"] = target
        record = validate_record({**base, **(declared_fields or {})})
        results.append(
            IngestResult(record=record, spans=spans, trajectory=format_trajectory(spans), source_kind="trace")
        )
    return results

def validate_record(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Check names and types. Unknown keys and bad types raise ``ValueError``.

    Absence is legal. This does not check that a translator mapped the
    right source field.
    """
    unknown = sorted(set(record) - set(RECORD_FIELDS))
    if unknown:
        shown = ", ".join(unknown)
        msg = f"Unknown sealed-record field(s): {shown}"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    checked: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in record.items():
        checked[key] = _check_field(key, value)
    return checked

docs.text:
Normalized multi-agent trace model and the derivations metrics read from it.

Source parsers (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, Patronus/TRAIL) map into Span. Everything below works on that shape alone, so no metric depends on a source format. Derivations are pure functions of the span list. Ground truth that no trace carries (gold roles, fault containment, baselines) is not here.

Adding a new source means writing one function, payload -> list[Span], and registering it in detect_and_parse. Each source's own kind vocabulary and shape differ enough (a flat list, OTLP's triple nesting, Patronus's recursive tree) that a single declarative mapping can't absorb all three, so each parser keeps its own walk, sharing only text_or_none and the Span/derivation contract below.

def validate_spans(spans: list[Span]) -> None:
    """Check ids are unique and every parent_id points at a span in the run."""
    ids = [span.id for span in spans]
    duplicates = sorted({sid for sid, count in Counter(ids).items() if count > 1})
    if duplicates:
        msg = f"duplicate span id(s): {', '.join(duplicates)}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    known = set(ids)
    for span in spans:
        if span.parent_id is not None and span.parent_id not in known:
            msg = f"span {span.id!r}: parent {span.parent_id!r} is not in the run"
            raise ValueError(msg)

def derive_agents(spans: list[Span]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """One entry per agent, with the tool and llm spans it owned as its step count."""
    validate_spans(spans)
    index = _by_id(spans)
    names = sorted({span.agent for span in spans if span.kind == "agent" and span.agent})
    steps: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for span in spans:
        if span.kind in ("tool", "llm"):
            owner = _nearest_agent_ancestor(span, index)
            if owner is not None:
                steps[owner] += 1
    return [{"id": name, "steps": steps[name]} for name in names]

def derive_delegations(spans: list[Span]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Agent spans whose parent is a different agent's span: one handoff each."""
    validate_spans(spans)
    index = _by_id(spans)
    handoffs = []
    for span in spans:
        if span.kind != "agent" or not span.agent or span.parent_id is None:
            continue
        parent = index[span.parent_id]
        sender = _nearest_agent_ancestor(parent, index)
        if sender is not None and sender != span.agent:
            handoffs.append({"sender": sender, "recipient": span.agent, "text": span.input})
    return handoffs

def derive_messages(spans: list[Span]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return delegations plus explicit message spans.

    A message span has no derivable recipient (open question 5), so it is None.
    """
    messages = [
        {"sender": d["sender"], "recipient": d["recipient"], "text": d["text"]} for d in derive_delegations(spans)
    ]
    for span in spans:
        if span.kind == "message":
            messages.append({"sender": span.agent, "recipient": None, "text": span.output})
    return messages

def derive_stall_evidence(spans: list[Span], threshold: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Identical repeated tool or llm calls under one agent, at or above ``threshold``.

    The threshold is declared. This returns evidence only; the declared
    ``run_stalled`` flag is what a metric grades.
    """
    if threshold < 2:
        msg = "stall threshold must be at least 2"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    validate_spans(spans)
    index = _by_id(spans)
    groups: Counter[tuple[str, str, str]] = Counter()
    for span in spans:
        if span.kind in ("tool", "llm"):
            owner = _nearest_agent_ancestor(span, index)
            if owner is not None:
                groups[(owner, span.kind, span.input or "")] += 1
    return [
        {"agent": agent, "kind": kind, "input": text, "count": count}
        for (agent, kind, text), count in sorted(groups.items())
        if count >= threshold
    ]

docs.text:
format_trajectory(spans, *, max_field_chars=2000)

Return an ordered, readable trace of the steps taken, for a judge to read.

Source-agnostic: works on any parser's output, since trajectory_optimality's judge only needs plain text (same shape as extract_trajectory_langfuse). Spans list order is used as step order. A span with no input and no output is skipped, the same discipline _format_step already uses for Langfuse's own equivalent.

max_field_chars Cap each span's input/output text at this many characters. Real instrumentation (e.g. an LLM-call span's logged input) routinely embeds the full system prompt plus the entire prior conversation so far on every step; uncapped, that makes the joined trajectory text grow roughly with the square of step count. On a real multi-step agent trace that reaches tens of thousands of tokens, which is slow to judge and can blow past a judge model's effective context. Each field is truncated to its leading max_field_chars characters with a marker noting how much was cut; short fields (the common case in tests and small traces) are unaffected.

Source code in src/aixeval/ingest/trace.py 
def format_trajectory(spans: list[Span], *, max_field_chars: int = 2000) -> str | None:
    """Return an ordered, readable trace of the steps taken, for a judge to read.

    Source-agnostic: works on any parser's output, since ``trajectory_optimality``'s
    judge only needs plain text (same shape as ``extract_trajectory_langfuse``).
    Spans list order is used as step order. A span with no input and no
    output is skipped, the same discipline ``_format_step`` already uses
    for Langfuse's own equivalent.

    max_field_chars
        Cap each span's ``input``/``output`` text at this many characters.
        Real instrumentation (e.g. an LLM-call span's logged ``input``)
        routinely embeds the full system prompt plus the entire prior
        conversation so far on every step; uncapped, that makes the
        joined trajectory text grow roughly with the square of step
        count. On a real multi-step agent trace that reaches tens of
        thousands of tokens, which is slow to judge and can blow past a
        judge model's effective context. Each field is truncated to its
        leading ``max_field_chars`` characters with a marker noting how
        much was cut; short fields (the common case in tests and small
        traces) are unaffected.
    """
    validate_spans(spans)
    lines: list[str] = []
    for index, span in enumerate(spans, start=1):
        if span.input is None and span.output is None:
            continue
        label = f"[{span.source_type}]" if span.source_type else f"[{span.kind}]"
        who = f" {span.agent}" if span.agent else ""
        parts = [f"{index}. {label}{who}"]
        if span.input is not None:
            parts.append(f"input: {_truncate_field(span.input, max_field_chars)}")
        if span.output is not None:
            parts.append(f"output: {_truncate_field(span.output, max_field_chars)}")
        lines.append(" -- ".join(parts))
    return "\n".join(lines) if lines else None

def detect_and_parse(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Span]:
    """Pick the right parser for ``payload``'s shape, then parse.

    Checked in this order: Langfuse (an ``observations`` list), OTLP
    (a ``resourceSpans`` list), tau-bench (a ``traj`` list), then
    Patronus/TRAIL (a ``spans`` list), Patronus last, since its
    top-level key is the most generic-looking of the four. Raises
    ``ValueError`` if none match.
    """
    from aixeval.ingest.trace_langfuse import parse_langfuse_trace  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.ingest.trace_otel import parse_otel_trace  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.ingest.trace_patronus import parse_patronus_trace  # noqa: PLC0415
    from aixeval.ingest.trace_taubench import parse_taubench_trace  # noqa: PLC0415

    if isinstance(payload.get("observations"), list):
        return parse_langfuse_trace(payload)
    if isinstance(payload.get("resourceSpans"), list):
        return parse_otel_trace(payload)
    if isinstance(payload.get("traj"), list):
        return parse_taubench_trace(payload)
    if isinstance(payload.get("spans"), list):
        return parse_patronus_trace(payload)
    msg = "payload did not match a known trace shape (Langfuse/OTel/Patronus/tau-bench)"
    raise ValueError(msg)

docs.title: trace_inspect
docs.text:
Map an Inspect AI .eval log into the normalized trace model.

A .eval file is a Zstd-compressed zip archive (header.json plus one samples/<id>_epoch_<n>.json per sample/epoch pair), not a plain JSON payload like Langfuse/OTel/Patronus: read_inspect_eval handles the archive layer, parse_inspect_sample maps one already-parsed sample dict to spans. zipfile's stdlib decompressor doesn't support Zstd on this project's Python version; zipfile_zstd is imported for its side effect of registering it (compression method 93) with zipfile directly, so zipfile.ZipFile(...).read(...) works normally afterward.

Built from sample["messages"] (Inspect's flattened, fully-resolved chat history), not the richer raw sample["events"] stream; events store conversation content via index-range references into a shared attachment buffer this parser doesn't resolve, while messages already carry plain text or a structured tool call directly. A real, stated asymmetry: per-step timing, exact sandbox exit codes, and span_begin/span_end nesting are not captured here, only each turn's text and each tool call's name, arguments, and returned text, same "stated honestly, not hidden" discipline as every other parser's documented gap in this module.

Single-agent only: nothing in a Inspect sample names a sub-agent the way Langfuse's gen_ai.agent.name or an OTel invoke_agent span does, so every span here is kind="llm" or kind="tool", never "agent": derive_delegations/derive_faults correctly find nothing, and the four MAS metrics correctly report N/A rather than a guessed delegation.

def read_inspect_eval(
    data: bytes,
    *,
    max_sample_bytes: int = MAX_SAMPLE_BYTES,
    max_total_bytes: int = MAX_TOTAL_BYTES,
    max_entries: int = MAX_SAMPLE_ENTRIES,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return every sample/epoch record a ``.eval`` file contains.

    Sorted by ``(sample id, epoch)`` so callers get a stable, predictable
    order: one dataset sample run for several epochs appears as
    consecutive entries, not shuffled by zip member order.

    Decompressed sizes are enforced while reading, not taken from the zip
    header (which an attacker controls), so a crafted archive cannot
    exhaust memory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data
        Raw bytes of the ``.eval`` file.
    max_sample_bytes
        Largest decompressed size allowed for one ``samples/*.json`` entry.
    max_total_bytes
        Largest decompressed size allowed across all sample entries.
    max_entries
        Most ``samples/*.json`` entries allowed.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Not a zip archive, it has no ``samples/*.json`` entries, or it
        exceeds one of the size/entry caps.
    """
    import zipfile_zstd  # noqa: F401,PLC0415 (side effect: registers Zstd with zipfile)

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
            names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.startswith("samples/") and n.endswith(".json")]
            if not names:
                msg = "no samples/*.json entries found in this .eval file"
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if len(names) > max_entries:
                msg = f".eval file has {len(names)} sample entries, more than the limit of {max_entries}"
                raise ValueError(msg)
            samples = []
            total = 0
            for name in names:
                raw = _read_capped(archive, name, max_sample_bytes)
                total += len(raw)
                if total > max_total_bytes:
                    msg = f".eval samples decompress to more than the limit of {max_total_bytes} bytes"
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                samples.append(json.loads(raw))
    except zipfile.BadZipFile as exc:
        msg = "not a valid .eval file (expected a zip archive)"
        raise ValueError(msg) from exc

    samples.sort(key=lambda s: (s.get("id"), s.get("epoch", 0)))
    return samples

def parse_inspect_sample(sample: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Span]:
    """Return normalized spans for one Inspect sample's message trace.

    One span per assistant turn (``kind="llm"``, ``output`` is its text)
    and per tool response (``kind="tool"``, ``input`` is the triggering
    call's ``function(arguments)``, ``output`` is the returned text).
    System/user messages (the task prompt) are not spans, same as every
    other parser here never keeping the raw prompt as a step.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``sample`` has no ``messages`` list.
    """
    messages = sample.get("messages")
    if not isinstance(messages, list):
        msg = "Inspect sample has no messages list"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    tool_calls_by_id = _index_tool_calls(messages)
    spans: list[Span] = []
    for index, message in enumerate(messages):
        if not isinstance(message, dict):
            continue
        role = message.get("role")
        if role == "assistant":
            spans.append(Span(id=f"msg{index}", kind="llm", output=_message_text(message.get("content"))))
        elif role == "tool":
            call_id = message.get("tool_call_id")
            call = tool_calls_by_id.get(call_id) if isinstance(call_id, str) else None
            spans.append(
                Span(
                    id=f"msg{index}",
                    kind="tool",
                    input=_tool_call_text(call) if call else None,
                    output=_message_text(message.get("content")),
                )
            )
    validate_spans(spans)
    return spans

Map an OpenTelemetry OTLP JSON export into the normalized trace model.

Targets raw OTLP traces that never passed through Langfuse. Uses the OTLP JSON field names (camelCase) and the GenAI semantic-convention attributes gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.agent.name. The GenAI agent attributes are still provisional in the OTel spec, so this parser is tied to today's attribute names and should be re-checked when that spec changes.

Delegation text is not captured: input and output are None, so any metric that needs handoff text reports N/A rather than guessing.

def parse_otel_trace(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Span]:
    """Return the normalized spans for one OTLP JSON trace, validated.

    Rejects payloads that contain more than one trace id, since one run is
    one trace.
    """
    resource_spans = payload.get("resourceSpans")
    if not isinstance(resource_spans, list):
        msg = "OTLP payload has no resourceSpans list"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    raw_spans = [
        span
        for resource in resource_spans
        for scope in _list(resource.get("scopeSpans"))
        for span in _list(scope.get("spans"))
    ]
    trace_ids = {span.get("traceId") for span in raw_spans if isinstance(span, dict)}
    if len(trace_ids) > 1:
        msg = f"OTLP payload holds {len(trace_ids)} trace ids; one run is one trace"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    spans: list[Span] = []
    for raw in raw_spans:
        spans.extend(_spans_from(raw))
    validate_spans(spans)
    return spans

Map a Patronus/TRAIL-shaped export into the normalized trace model.

Verified against a real export: one top-level span per trace, with the real run nested under child_spans, not a flat span list like Langfuse or raw OTLP. Span kind comes from span_attributes["openinference.span.kind"]; the top-level span_kind field is always "Internal" and carries no information.

No agent identity: OpenInference has no dedicated agent-name attribute, and this export's framework (smolagents) only puts a sub-agent's name in its own prompt text or in the parent's smolagents.managed_agents.*.name attribute; neither is a general rule. agent is left None here rather than guessed; a framework-specific extractor could be added later if needed.

def parse_patronus_trace(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Span]:
    """Return the normalized spans for one Patronus/TRAIL export, validated."""
    roots = payload.get("spans")
    if not isinstance(roots, list) or not roots:
        msg = "Patronus payload has no spans list"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    spans: list[Span] = []
    for root in roots:
        _walk(root, spans)
    validate_spans(spans)
    return spans

docs.title: trace_taubench
docs.text:
Map a tau-bench episode's flat chat trajectory into the normalized trace model.

tau-bench (sierra-research/tau-bench, MIT licensed) ships each episode as {"task_id", "reward", "info": {...}, "traj": [...]}. traj is a flat OpenAI-chat-format message list: role in system/user/ assistant/tool, an assistant message either carrying tool_calls ([{"id", "function": {"name", "arguments"}}]) or plain text content, and a tool message pairing back to its call via tool_call_id.

Unlike Langfuse/OTel/Patronus, there is no explicit span tree here: one flat message list for one single support agent. This parser reconstructs the shape the rest of the toolkit expects: one top-level "agent" span (its input is every user-turn text joined, its output is the final text-only assistant reply) plus one "tool" span per tool call and one "llm" span per text-only assistant reply, both parented to the agent span. The agent span is returned last, not first: trajectory_optimality reads span order as step order (see format_trajectory), and the agent's own summary line is not a step that happened before the tool calls and replies that produced it.

A harness-dependent serialization quirk, live-confirmed across tau-bench's own shipped historical_trajectories: GPT-4o's tool_calls[].function. arguments is a JSON string; Sonnet's is already a native dict. Both are handled explicitly below (_args_text): no blind json.loads, no silent except Exception swallowing a real TypeError (that broad except masked this exact bug once already, in the scratch pilot this parser was promoted from).

def parse_taubench_trace(payload: dict[str, Any], *, agent_name: str = DEFAULT_AGENT_NAME) -> list[Span]:
    """Return the normalized spans for one tau-bench episode, validated.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        A tau-bench episode dict (or just its ``{"traj": [...]}`` shape,
        callers typically pass ``episode`` itself, since ``task_id``/
        ``reward``/``info`` are ignored here; declared ground truth like
        ``gold_tool_calls`` belongs in ``ingest_any``'s ``declared_fields``,
        not auto-extracted by this parser).
    agent_name
        tau-bench's own episodes don't declare a name for the single
        support agent; defaulted rather than guessed from the system
        prompt's free text.
    """
    traj = payload.get("traj")
    if not isinstance(traj, list):
        msg = "tau-bench payload has no traj list"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    tool_results = _tool_results_by_call_id(traj)
    spans: list[Span] = []
    user_texts: list[str] = []
    last_reply: str | None = None
    for index, message in enumerate(traj):
        if not isinstance(message, dict):
            continue
        role = message.get("role")
        if role == "user":
            text = text_or_none(message.get("content"))
            if text:
                user_texts.append(text)
            continue
        if role != "assistant":
            continue
        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
        if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
            spans.extend(_tool_spans(index, tool_calls, tool_results))
            continue
        text = text_or_none(message.get("content"))
        if not text:
            continue
        spans.append(Span(id=f"llm:{index}", kind="llm", parent_id=AGENT_SPAN_ID, output=text))
        last_reply = text
    spans.append(
        Span(
            id=AGENT_SPAN_ID,
            kind="agent",
            agent=agent_name,
            input="\n\n".join(user_texts) or None,
            output=last_reply,
        )
    )
    validate_spans(spans)
    return spans

def extract_tool_calls_taubench(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Pull the actual tool calls a tau-bench episode made, as structured data.

    Mirrors ``extract_tool_calls_langfuse``: walks the raw payload (not the
    parsed ``Span`` list) and reshapes to ``{"tool": <name>, "args": <dict>}``,
    ready to compare against a declared ``gold_tool_calls`` list with no LLM
    involved, via ``run_tool_call_accuracy_check``.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict] | None
        One entry per tool call, in order, or ``None`` if there were none.
    """
    traj = payload.get("traj")
    if not isinstance(traj, list):
        return None
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for message in traj:
        if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
            continue
        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
        if not isinstance(tool_calls, list):
            continue
        for call in tool_calls:
            if not isinstance(call, dict):
                continue
            function = call.get("function")
            if not isinstance(function, dict):
                continue
            name = function.get("name")
            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                continue
            calls.append({"tool": name, "args": _args_dict(function.get("arguments"))})
    return calls or None
