def print_taubench_example() -> None:
    """Print the spans parsed from one small, hand-built tau-bench episode."""
    episode = {
        "traj": [
            {"role": "system", "content": "You are a retail support agent."},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Please cancel order #100 and refund to gift card."},
            {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": None,
                "tool_calls": [
                    {"id": "call_1", "function": {"name": "cancel_pending_order", "arguments": '{"order_id": "#100"}'}}
                ],
            },
            {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": '{"status": "cancelled"}'},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "Order #100 has been cancelled and refunded to your gift card."},
        ]
    }
    for span in parse_taubench_trace(episode):
        print(f"  {span.id}: kind={span.kind} source_type={span.source_type} input={span.input} output={span.output}")
    print(f"  tool calls: {extract_tool_calls_taubench(episode)}")

class ClaudeClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one Claude call. Prompt in, text out. No judge logic."""

    def __init__(self, *, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._client = client if client is not None else anthropic.Anthropic()

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the first text block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user message. No system prompt or judge framing here.
        max_tokens
            Passed straight to the API.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The first text content block in the reply.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
        """
        response = self._client.messages.create(
            model=self._model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        for block in response.content:
            if block.type == "text":
                return block.text
        msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image, return the first text block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user message.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF), base64-encoded
            and sent as an image content block alongside ``prompt``.
        max_tokens
            Passed straight to the API.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The first text content block in the reply.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
        """
        image_block: ImageBlockParam = {
            "type": "image",
            "source": {
                "type": "base64",
                "media_type": guess_mime_type(image_path),
                "data": read_image_base64(image_path),
            },
        }
        text_block: TextBlockParam = {"type": "text", "text": prompt}
        message: MessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [image_block, text_block]}
        response = self._client.messages.create(
            model=self._model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=[message],
        )
        for block in response.content:
            if block.type == "text":
                return block.text
        msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
        raise ValueError(msg)

class GeminiClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one Gemini generate_content call. Prompt in, text out."""

    def __init__(self, *, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, client: genai.Client | None = None) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._client = client if client is not None else genai.Client()

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``config.max_output_tokens``.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.text``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. blocked by safety settings).
        """
        response = self._client.models.generate_content(
            model=self._model,
            contents=prompt,
            config=types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0),
        )
        text = response.text
        if not text:
            msg = "Gemini reply had no text"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        return text

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image, return the plain text reply.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file, read as raw bytes and sent as
            an inline ``types.Part`` alongside ``prompt``.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``config.max_output_tokens``.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.text``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. blocked by safety settings).
        """
        image_part = types.Part.from_bytes(data=Path(image_path).read_bytes(), mime_type=guess_mime_type(image_path))
        # list[Any]: the SDK's generate_content overloads for a mixed
        # [Part, str] list don't unify cleanly under mypy's invariant
        # list generics (see its own `Content | ContentDict | str |
        # Image | ... | list[...]` union); Any is the least-bad
        # escape hatch here, not a blanket suppression.
        contents: list[Any] = [image_part, prompt]
        response = self._client.models.generate_content(
            model=self._model,
            contents=contents,
            config=types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0),
        )
        text = response.text
        if not text:
            msg = "Gemini reply had no text"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        return text

class OpenAIClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one OpenAI Responses API call. Prompt in, text out."""

    def __init__(self, *, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, client: openai.OpenAI | None = None) -> None:

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Uses the Responses API (``client.responses.create``), the surface
        OpenAI's own SDK README lists first for single-turn text requests.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input. No system/instructions framing here.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_output_tokens``. Unlike the Claude client,
            this parameter name is not confirmed against a pinned
            reference doc for this SDK; verify against the installed
            ``openai`` package if a request rejects it.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.output_text``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. blocked or empty).
        """
        response = self._client.responses.create(
            model=self._model,
            input=prompt,
            max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
        )
        text = response.output_text
        if not text:
            msg = "OpenAI reply had no text"
            raise ValueError(msg)

class CapturingProvider:
    """Wraps a Provider, stashing the last raw reply for the attachment.

    judge_grounding only returns the parsed score, by design (it has to
    stay a plain ``Callable[[str, str], float]`` to match
    ``score_grounding``'s existing seam). This wrapper is how the
    runner still gets the raw reply for the attachment, without
    changing that contract. Public: also reused by
    ``aixeval.ui.logic`` to surface a live judge's reasoning text
    in the UI, same reason: the ``judge_*`` functions only return a
    parsed score.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: Provider) -> None:
        self._inner = inner
        self.last_reply: str | None = None

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider's model id."""
        return self._inner.model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider, stashing the reply first."""
        reply = self._inner.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        self.last_reply = reply
        return reply

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider, stashing the reply first."""
        reply = self._inner.complete_with_image(prompt, image_path, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        self.last_reply = reply
        return reply

class VLLMClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one Chat Completions call to a self-hosted vLLM server.

    vLLM's server implements the OpenAI Chat Completions surface, not
    the newer Responses API ``OpenAIClient`` uses.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        model: str,
        client: openai.OpenAI | None = None,
        base_url_env_var: str = BASE_URL_ENV_VAR,
        api_key_env_var: str = API_KEY_ENV_VAR,
        send_temperature: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Build a client for a self-hosted vLLM server.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model
            Whatever model id the server was started with. vLLM serves
            exactly one model per process, so there is no toolkit-wide
            default the way hosted providers have one.
        client
            An already-built ``openai.OpenAI`` to use instead of
            constructing one from ``base_url_env_var``/``api_key_env_var``
            (e.g. for tests, or a non-standard auth setup).
        base_url_env_var
            Which environment variable names the server's base URL.
            Read at construction time, default ``http://localhost:8000/v1``
            if unset.
        api_key_env_var
            Which environment variable names the API key, if the server
            was started with ``--api-key``. Unset is fine: a placeholder
            value is sent instead, since the ``openai`` SDK requires a
            non-empty string but vLLM without ``--api-key`` ignores it.
        send_temperature
            Defaults on, ``temperature=0`` for reproducibility. Set
            ``False`` for a model/server combination that rejects an
            explicit temperature, same gotcha already documented for
            OpenAI's and Vector's reasoning-tier models.
        """
        self._model = model
        self._send_temperature = send_temperature
        base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_env_var, DEFAULT_BASE_URL)
        api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_env_var) or _UNUSED_API_KEY
        self._client = client if client is not None else openai.OpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key)

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_tokens`` on the Chat Completions call.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.choices[0].message.content``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. no choices, or empty content).
        """
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"temperature": 0} if self._send_temperature else {}
        response = self._client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self._model,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            **kwargs,
        )
        return _text_from_chat_response(response)

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image via Chat Completions' multimodal content.

        Whether this actually works depends on the deployed model being
        vision-capable (e.g. a Qwen-VL or LLaVA checkpoint); a text-only
        model errors on this call instead, surfacing to the caller like
        any other judge-call failure, not silently.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file, base64-encoded into a data URL.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_tokens`` on the Chat Completions call.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.choices[0].message.content``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. no choices, or empty content).
        """
        data_url = f"data:{guess_mime_type(image_path)};base64,{read_image_base64(image_path)}"
        text_part: ChatCompletionContentPartTextParam = {"type": "text", "text": prompt}
        image_part: ChatCompletionContentPartImageParam = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}}
        message: ChatCompletionUserMessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [text_part, image_part]}
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"temperature": 0} if self._send_temperature else {}
        response = self._client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self._model,
            messages=[message],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            **kwargs,
        )
        return _text_from_chat_response(response)

def extract_tool_calls_taubench(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Pull the actual tool calls a tau-bench episode made, as structured data.

    Mirrors ``extract_tool_calls_langfuse``: walks the raw payload (not the
    parsed ``Span`` list) and reshapes to ``{"tool": <name>, "args": <dict>}``,
    ready to compare against a declared ``gold_tool_calls`` list with no LLM
    involved, via ``run_tool_call_accuracy_check``.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict] | None
        One entry per tool call, in order, or ``None`` if there were none.
    """
    traj = payload.get("traj")
    if not isinstance(traj, list):
        return None
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for message in traj:
        if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
            continue
        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
        if not isinstance(tool_calls, list):
            continue
        for call in tool_calls:
            if not isinstance(call, dict):
                continue
            function = call.get("function")
            if not isinstance(function, dict):
                continue
            name = function.get("name")
            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                continue
            calls.append({"tool": name, "args": _args_dict(function.get("arguments"))})
    return calls or None

def judge_abstention(output: str, client: Provider, *, max_tokens: int = 4000) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` to grade whether ``output`` appropriately abstains, on ``[0, 1]``.

    Matches the ``AbstentionJudge`` shape ``score_abstention`` already
    accepts (``Callable[[str], float]``) once ``client`` is bound, e.g.
    ``functools.partial(judge_abstention, client=my_client)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output
        What the system under test actually said.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``. Needs real headroom: a
        reasoning-capable model can spend most of this budget on its
        own reasoning before ever emitting the final ``SCORE:`` line.
        Default of 4000 matches the value confirmed live against the
        Vector reasoning model (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed
        to fail with ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on a real call.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(output=output)
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return parse_score(reply)

def build_client(provider: str, model: str | None = None) -> Provider:
    """Build a judge client for an explicitly chosen provider and model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    provider
        One of ``available_providers()``; case and surrounding spaces
        are ignored.
    model
        The model id to send. ``None`` or blank falls back to
        ``default_model_for(provider)``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``provider`` is not one this toolkit knows, or it has no
        default model (``vllm``) and none was given or set in its env var.
    NotImplementedError
        The named provider is known but has no client wired up
        (defensive only; every declared provider currently is).
    """
    provider = provider.strip().lower()
    if provider not in _MODEL_ENV_VARS:
        known = ", ".join(sorted(_MODEL_ENV_VARS))
        msg = f"Unknown {PROVIDER_ENV_VAR}={provider!r}. Known providers: {known}."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    build = _BUILDERS.get(provider)
    if build is None:
        msg = f"Provider {provider!r} is declared but has no client yet."
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)
    chosen = (model or "").strip() or default_model_for(provider)
    if not chosen:
        model_env_var = _MODEL_ENV_VARS[provider]
        msg = f"Set {model_env_var} to name the model your {provider} server is serving; there is no default."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return build(chosen)

def judge_cross_modal_hallucination(
    output: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    image_description: str | None = None,
    image_path: str | None = None,
    max_tokens: int = 4000,
) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` to grade whether ``output`` hallucinates against the image.

    Exactly one of ``image_description``/``image_path`` must be
    passed. With ``image_description``, the judge reads a declared
    text proxy via ``client.complete``. With ``image_path``, the
    judge reads the real image via ``client.complete_with_image``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output
        What the system under test actually said.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    image_description
        A declared text description of what the image actually shows.
        Mutually exclusive with ``image_path``.
    image_path
        Path to the real image file. Mutually exclusive with
        ``image_description``. Whether the call succeeds depends on
        ``client`` being backed by a vision-capable model; see each
        ``Provider``'s ``complete_with_image`` docstring.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``/``client.complete_with_image``.
        Needs real headroom: a reasoning-capable model can spend most
        of this budget on its own reasoning before ever emitting the
        final ``SCORE:`` line. Default of 4000 matches the value
        confirmed live against the Vector reasoning model
        (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed to fail with
        ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on real traces.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``. Lower is better: 0 is no
        hallucination, 1 is substantially hallucinated.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Neither or both of ``image_description``/``image_path`` were
        passed, or the reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:``
        line.
    """
    if (image_description is None) == (image_path is None):
        msg = "Pass exactly one of image_description or image_path, not both or neither."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if image_path is not None:
        prompt = _IMAGE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(output=output)
        reply = client.complete_with_image(prompt, image_path, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    else:
        prompt = _DESCRIPTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(image_description=image_description, output=output)
        reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return parse_score(reply)

def extract_tool_calls_langfuse(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Pull the actual tool calls a Langfuse-shaped run made, as structured data.

    Filters the same ``observations`` list ``extract_trajectory_langfuse``
    reads down to ``type == "TOOL"`` entries only, reshaped as
    ``{"tool": <name>, "args": <input>}``, ready to compare against a
    declared ``gold_tool_calls`` list with no LLM involved.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict] | None
        One entry per tool call, in order, or ``None`` if there were
        none. A tool call with no usable ``name`` is skipped; a missing
        ``input`` becomes ``{}``, never ``None``, so downstream
        comparison never has to special-case it.
    """
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if not isinstance(observations, list):
        return None
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for item in observations:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("type") != "TOOL":
            continue
        name = item.get("name")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            continue
        args = item.get("input")
        calls.append({"tool": name, "args": args if isinstance(args, dict) else {}})
    return calls or None

def extract_trajectory_langfuse(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Pull an ordered, readable trace of the steps a Langfuse-shaped run took.

    Walks the same ``observations`` list ``extract_evidence_langfuse``
    reads, but pulls ``type``/``name``/``input``/``output`` per step
    instead of just ``input``: a trace of what happened, not evidence
    for what the answer should say.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        One numbered line per observation, or ``None`` if there were
        none.
    """
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if not isinstance(observations, list):
        return None
    lines: list[str] = []
    for index, item in enumerate(observations, start=1):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        line = _format_step(index, item)
        if line is not None:
            lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines) if lines else None

def extract_live_grounding_evidence(
    payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    spans: list[Span] | None = None,
) -> str | None:
    """Return the evidence text live grounding should judge against.

    Langfuse-shaped dumps use ``extract_evidence_langfuse``, the same
    extractor ``run_grounding_judge`` takes. Other traces fall back to
    span input texts (``collect_trace_input_texts``): what the agent
    saw, not the step log ``format_trajectory`` builds. Trajectory
    text is never used. ``None`` when neither source has usable input.
    """
    if payload is not None and isinstance(payload.get("observations"), list):
        from_dump = extract_evidence_langfuse(payload)
        if from_dump:
            return from_dump
    if spans:
        texts = collect_trace_input_texts(spans)
        return "\n\n".join(texts) if texts else None
    return None

def live_judge_is_possible(
    metric_id: str,
    record: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    trajectory: str | None,
    image_path: str | None,
    evidence: str | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """Report whether ``run_live_judges`` would actually attempt this metric now.

    Checks the exact same preconditions ``run_live_judges`` itself uses
    (output present, plus the metric's own ``LiveJudgeSpec.possible``) --
    without making a judge call or needing a real client/API key.

    spec = LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS.get(metric_id)
    if spec is None:

    output = record.get("output")

        output=output,
        trajectory=trajectory,
        evidence=evidence,
        image_path=image_path,
        capturing=CapturingProvider(_UnreachableProvider()),
    )
    return spec.possible(ctx)

Run a live judge call for each selected metric this dispatcher supports.

Returns (updated_record, rationale_by_metric, error_by_metric). updated_record is a copy of record with each successful verdict's field set. A metric that needed a trajectory, evidence, or image that isn't available is silently skipped (the later scorer call reports it N/A, same as any other missing-evidence case); that is not an error. A judge call that raises anything (a bad reply, or a provider SDK error such as a rate limit, auth failure or timeout, none of which subclass ValueError/ OSError) is caught per metric so one failing judge never blocks the others; its message lands in error_by_metric instead of crashing the run.

A metric whose record_field is already on record is not re-judged: a saved verdict (a replayed scenario) is reused rather than spending another call. Each new verdict also writes judge_provenance for that metric (model + prompt version).

Source code in src/aixeval/judge/live.py 
def run_live_judges(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    trajectory: str | None,
    image_path: str | None,
    selected_ids: set[str],
    client: Provider,
    evidence: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    """Run a live judge call for each selected metric this dispatcher supports.

    Returns ``(updated_record, rationale_by_metric, error_by_metric)``.
    ``updated_record`` is a copy of ``record`` with each successful
    verdict's field set. A metric that needed a trajectory, evidence,
    or image that isn't available is silently skipped (the later
    scorer call reports it N/A, same as any other missing-evidence
    case); that is not an error. A judge call that raises anything (a
    bad reply, or a provider SDK error such as a rate limit, auth
    failure or timeout, none of which subclass ``ValueError``/
    ``OSError``) is caught per metric so one failing judge never
    blocks the others; its message lands in ``error_by_metric``
    instead of crashing the run.

    A metric whose ``record_field`` is already on ``record`` is not
    re-judged: a saved verdict (a replayed scenario) is reused rather
    than spending another call. Each new verdict also writes
    ``judge_provenance`` for that metric (model + prompt version).
    """
    updated = dict(record)
    rationale: dict[str, str] = {}
    errors: dict[str, str] = {}
    capturing = CapturingProvider(client)

    for metric_id in selected_ids & LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS.keys():
        spec = LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS[metric_id]
        if spec.record_field in updated:
            continue
        output = updated.get("output")
        if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
            continue
        ctx = _JudgeCallArgs(
            record=updated,
            output=output,
            trajectory=trajectory,
            evidence=evidence,
            image_path=image_path,
            capturing=capturing,
        )
        try:
            verdict = spec.run(ctx)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (any provider failure is isolated to this one metric)
            errors[metric_id] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            continue
        if verdict is None:
            continue
        updated[spec.record_field] = verdict
        updated = merge_judge_provenance(updated, metric_id, client, spec.prompt_version)
        if capturing.last_reply:
            rationale[metric_id] = capturing.last_reply.strip()[:500]
    return updated, rationale, errors

def suggest_relevant_metrics(
    description: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    metric_ids: Sequence[str] = ALL_METRIC_IDS,
    max_tokens: int = 6000,
    source_kind: str | None = None,
    has_trajectory: bool | None = None,
    num_distinct_agents: int | None = None,
    has_image: bool | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Ask ``client`` which of ``metric_ids`` are meaningful for this run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    description
        A short free-text summary of the run (domain, what the agent(s)
        did, and so on): what the person uploading it typed, not
        verified against the actual data.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    metric_ids
        Which metric ids to offer. Defaults to the full catalog
        (``ALL_METRIC_IDS``: auto-wired and opt-in both).
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``. The catalog is long (44 lines by
        default), so this needs more headroom than a single-score judge.
        Default of 6000 is set from live testing against the Vector
        reasoning model (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``): at 2048 it spends the
        whole budget on internal reasoning before emitting any
        ``RELEVANT:`` lines and ``client.complete`` raises ``ValueError:
        ... had no text``. A faster/non-reasoning provider may need far
        less, but 6000 is a safe default across providers.
    source_kind, has_trajectory, num_distinct_agents, has_image
        Objective facts checked directly against the ingested record/
        spans; not re-derived from ``description``, which the caller
        may have misstated or left incomplete (e.g. forgot to mention a
        run is multi-agent, or that an image is attached). ``None`` means
        not known/not checked, and that fact is simply left out of the
        prompt rather than asserted as false. Pass these whenever an
        ``IngestResult`` already exists to check (the UI always does
        once something is ingested); omit them only when suggesting
        against a bare description with nothing ingested yet.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, str]
        ``{metric_id: reason}`` for every metric the model flagged
        relevant. A metric it did not mention is simply not suggested,
        not an error, and not a claim that the metric cannot be scored.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable ``RELEVANT:`` line naming a known
        metric id.
    """
    catalog = "\n".join(f"{metric_id}: {definition_for_any_metric(metric_id)}" for metric_id in metric_ids)
    facts_block = _format_facts(
        source_kind=source_kind,
        has_trajectory=has_trajectory,
        num_distinct_agents=num_distinct_agents,
        has_image=has_image,
    )
    # Only tell the model to trust RUN FACTS over the description when a
    # RUN FACTS section actually exists; otherwise this would be a
    # dangling reference to a section that was never rendered.
    facts_trust_note = (
        " Where RUN FACTS and RUN DESCRIPTION disagree, trust RUN FACTS: it is "
        "checked directly against the ingested data; the description is only what "
        "the person typed and may be incomplete or wrong."
        if facts_block
        else ""
    )
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
        description=description, facts_block=facts_block, facts_trust_note=facts_trust_note, catalog=catalog
    )
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return _parse_relevant(reply, known_ids=set(metric_ids))

def judge_pairwise_preference(
    output: str,
    baseline_output: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    reference: str | None = None,
    max_tokens: int = 4000,
) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` which of ``output``/``baseline_output`` is better, on ``[0, 1]``.

    Matches the ``PairwisePreferenceJudge`` shape
    ``score_pairwise_preference`` already accepts
    (``Callable[[str, str], float]``) once ``client`` (and optionally
    ``reference``) is bound, e.g.
    ``functools.partial(judge_pairwise_preference, client=my_client)``.

    Makes two judge calls, not one, to correct for position bias:
    once presenting ``output`` as RESPONSE A, once with the order
    swapped. The two preference scores are averaged. 1.0 means
    ``output`` won both presentations outright; 0.0 means it lost
    both; 0.5 is a genuine tie or a bias-cancelling split decision.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output
        The candidate response being scored.
    baseline_output
        The opponent response ``output`` is compared against.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    reference
        An optional gold/reference answer. When given, the judge is
        told to use it as a guide to correctness, not a strict
        template, the same spirit as AlpacaEval-style reference-
        anchored pairwise judging. When absent, the judge falls back
        to general helpfulness and correctness.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete`` on each of the two calls. Needs
        real headroom: a reasoning-capable model can spend most of
        this budget on its own reasoning before ever emitting the
        final ``SCORE:`` line. Default of 4000 matches the value
        confirmed live against the Vector reasoning model
        (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed to fail with
        ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on a real call.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The position-bias-corrected preference score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Either reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    forward = _compare(output, baseline_output, client, reference=reference, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    backward = _compare(baseline_output, output, client, reference=reference, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    # In the backward call, `output` is RESPONSE B, so its implied
    # preference there is (1 - backward)'s score for RESPONSE A.
    return (forward + (1.0 - backward)) / 2.0

def merge_judge_provenance(
    record: dict[str, Any], metric_id: str, client: Provider, prompt_version: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a copy of ``record`` with this metric's provenance set.

    Existing entries for other metrics are kept. An existing entry for

Distinct model ids recorded on record, in first-seen order.

def models_from_provenance(record: dict[str, Any] | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Distinct model ids recorded on ``record``, in first-seen order."""
    if not record:
        return ()
    raw = record.get(PROVENANCE_FIELD)
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return ()
    models: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry in raw.values():
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        model = entry.get("model")
        if isinstance(model, str) and model and model not in seen:
            seen.add(model)
            models.append(model)
    return tuple(models)

collect_rerun_scores(run_once, field, *, n=3)

Call a judge runner n times on one input, each time collecting one field.

The missing piece for scorecard.test_retest_stability, which only grades an already-assembled rerun_scores list; this is what actually assembles one, by making the repeated calls.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default run_once Callable[[], tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]

A zero-argument callable, already bound to a specific runner and input via functools.partial, e.g. functools.partial(run_grounding_judge, payload, record, client, extract_evidence_langfuse). Called n times, unchanged: this function does not cache or short-circuit repeated identical calls. That would defeat the point of a test-retest check: it exists to see whether a live judge call actually varies run to run.

required field str

Which field to read off each call's returned record, e.g. "grounding_judge".

required n int

How many times to call run_once. Default 3: the smallest number that can show a spread rather than just a pair.

3

Returns:

Type Description list[float]

One score per call that succeeded (attachment["status"] == "scored"). A call that fails is silently excluded, not counted as a 0.0; the same N/A discipline every other metric in this toolkit already follows. Pass the result straight to scorecard.test_retest_stability's rerun_scores field; it treats fewer than 2 scores as N/A on its own.

Source code in src/aixeval/judge/runner.py 
def collect_rerun_scores(
    run_once: Callable[[], tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]],
    field: str,
    *,
    n: int = 3,
) -> list[float]:
    """Call a judge runner ``n`` times on one input, each time collecting one field.

    The missing piece for ``scorecard.test_retest_stability``, which
    only grades an already-assembled ``rerun_scores`` list; this is
    what actually assembles one, by making the repeated calls.

    Parameters
    ----------
    run_once
        A zero-argument callable, already bound to a specific runner
        and input via ``functools.partial``, e.g.
        ``functools.partial(run_grounding_judge, payload, record,
        client, extract_evidence_langfuse)``. Called ``n`` times,
        unchanged: this function does not cache or short-circuit
        repeated identical calls. That would defeat the point of a
        test-retest check: it exists to see whether a live judge call
        actually varies run to run.
    field
        Which field to read off each call's returned record, e.g.
        ``"grounding_judge"``.
    n
        How many times to call ``run_once``. Default 3: the smallest
        number that can show a spread rather than just a pair.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One score per call that succeeded (``attachment["status"] ==
        "scored"``). A call that fails is silently excluded, not
        counted as a 0.0; the same N/A discipline every other
        metric in this toolkit already follows. Pass the result
        straight to ``scorecard.test_retest_stability``'s
        ``rerun_scores`` field; it treats fewer than 2 scores as N/A
        on its own.
    """
    scores: list[float] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        new_record, attachment = run_once()
        if attachment.get("status") != "scored":
            continue
        value = new_record.get(field)
        if isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool):
            scores.append(float(value))
    return scores

def run_abstention_judge(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's abstention from ``output`` alone: no dump needed.

    Unlike ``run_grounding_judge``, there is no evidence to extract:
    the only input the judge needs, ``output``, already lives on the
    sealed record.

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record; ``output`` is read from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_abstention``. See
        ``run_grounding_judge``'s docstring for why this needs real
        headroom for reasoning-capable models.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``abstention_judge`` set. On failure,
        it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has ``status``
        (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``, ``prompt_version``,
        and ``timestamp``; ``reason`` when failed; ``raw_reply`` once a
        call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, ABSTENTION_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, reason="record has no output to judge"
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        score = judge_abstention(output, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            ABSTENTION_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason=f"judge call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    new_record = _record_with_verdict(
        record,
        field="abstention_judge",
        score=score,
        metric_id="abstention",
        client=client,
        prompt_version=ABSTENTION_PROMPT_VERSION,
    )
    attachment = _attachment("scored", client, ABSTENTION_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply)
    return new_record, attachment

def run_cross_modal_hallucination_judge(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's cross-modal hallucination from a declared description or path.

    No dump needed: ``image_path``/``image_description`` and
    ``output`` already live on the sealed record, same no-dump-needed
    discipline as ``run_abstention_judge``/``run_refusal_judge``.
    Prefers ``image_path`` (the judge reads the real image) over
    ``image_description`` (text proxy) when a record has both.

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record; ``image_path``/``image_description`` and
        ``output`` are read from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_cross_modal_hallucination``. See
        ``run_grounding_judge``'s docstring for why this needs real
        headroom for reasoning-capable models.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``cross_modal_hallucination_judge``
        set. On failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment
        always has ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``),
        ``model``, ``prompt_version``, and ``timestamp``; ``reason``
        when failed; ``raw_reply`` once a call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    image_path = record.get("image_path")
    image_description = record.get("image_description")
    has_image_path = isinstance(image_path, str) and bool(image_path.strip())
    has_image_description = isinstance(image_description, str) and bool(image_description.strip())
    if not has_image_path and not has_image_description:
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            CROSS_MODAL_HALLUCINATION_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="record has no image_path or image_description to judge against",
        )

    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            CROSS_MODAL_HALLUCINATION_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="record has no output to judge",
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        if has_image_path:
            score = judge_cross_modal_hallucination(output, wrapped, image_path=image_path, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        else:
            score = judge_cross_modal_hallucination(
                output, wrapped, image_description=image_description, max_tokens=max_tokens
            )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            CROSS_MODAL_HALLUCINATION_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason=f"judge call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    new_record = _record_with_verdict(
        record,
        field="cross_modal_hallucination_judge",
        score=score,
        metric_id="cross_modal_hallucination",
        client=client,
        prompt_version=CROSS_MODAL_HALLUCINATION_PROMPT_VERSION,
    )
    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored", client, CROSS_MODAL_HALLUCINATION_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply
    )
    return new_record, attachment

def run_grounding_judge(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    extract_evidence: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], str | None],
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's grounding against evidence pulled from its raw dump.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        The original dump, already loaded from JSON, not the sealed
        record. Evidence lives here; ingest's copy-only rule already
        stripped it out of ``record``.
    record
        The sealed record; ``output`` is read from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    extract_evidence
        Which evidence extractor to use for this dump's shape, e.g.
        ``extract_evidence_langfuse``. The caller picks it explicitly;
        no auto-detection, same discipline as ingest.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_grounding``. The default matches
        ``judge_grounding`` (4000). Raise this when evidence is large;
        there is no automatic scaling here.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``grounding_judge`` set. On failure, it
        is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has ``status``
        (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``, ``prompt_version``,
        and ``timestamp``; ``evidence_excerpt`` once evidence exists;
        ``reason`` when failed; ``raw_reply`` once a call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    evidence = extract_evidence(payload)
    if evidence is None:
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, reason="no evidence extracted from the dump"
        )

    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, evidence=evidence, reason="record has no output to judge"
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        score = judge_grounding(evidence, output, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            evidence=evidence,
            reason=f"judge call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    new_record = _record_with_verdict(
        record,
        field="grounding_judge",
        score=score,
        metric_id="grounding",
        client=client,
        prompt_version=PROMPT_VERSION,
    )
    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, evidence=evidence, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply
    )
    return new_record, attachment

def run_pairwise_preference_judge(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,

    """Judge one record's ``output`` against a declared ``baseline_output``.

    No dump needed: both texts already live on the sealed record,
    same discipline as ``run_abstention_judge``/``run_refusal_judge``.
    If ``expected`` (a gold reference) is present, it is passed to the
    judge as optional context. Unlike every other runner here, the
    judge makes two model calls per verdict, not one: position-bias
    correction, averaging over both presentation orders (see
    ``aixeval.judge.pairwise_preference``).

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record; ``output``, ``baseline_output``, and
        (optionally) ``expected`` are read from it. Never mutated.
    client

    max_tokens

        ``run_grounding_judge``'s docstring for why this needs real
        headroom for reasoning-capable models.

        copy of ``record`` with ``pairwise_preference_judge`` set. On
        failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``,
        ``prompt_version``, and ``timestamp``; ``reason`` when failed;
        ``raw_reply`` (both calls' replies, joined) once at least one
        call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PAIRWISE_PREFERENCE_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, reason="record has no output to judge"
        )

    baseline = record.get("baseline_output")
    if not isinstance(baseline, str) or not baseline.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PAIRWISE_PREFERENCE_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="record has no baseline_output to compare against",
        )

    reference = record.get("expected")
    reference = reference if isinstance(reference, str) and reference.strip() else None

    wrapped = _ListCapturingProvider(client)
    try:

def run_protected_attribute_bias_detector(
    input_texts: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Scan a trace's own input text for a candidate protected-attribute signal.

    A detector, not a scorer: same spirit as
    ``aixeval.ingest.audit.audit_expected_in_inputs`` (contamination's
    auto-detect over trace input text) but semantic rather than
    deterministic, so it needs a real judge call and never writes a
    record field itself -- the candidate it returns is always a
    suggestion for a human to confirm or edit, never auto-applied. See
    ``aixeval.ui.logic.merge_bias_signal_into_declared`` for the step
    that turns a confirmed candidate into ``should_resist_bias`` /
    ``protected_attribute_signal`` declared fields.

    Parameters
    ----------
    input_texts
        Raw text pulled from the trace's own spans, typically
        ``aixeval.ingest.trace.collect_trace_input_texts(spans)``.
        Joined into one block before the call; empty/blank entries
        are dropped.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_detect_protected_attribute_signal``.
        Default is ``DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS`` so reasoning models
        (Qwen3) have headroom for hidden thinking before ``SIGNAL:``.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[str | None, dict]
        ``(candidate_signal, attachment)``. ``candidate_signal`` is
        ``None`` when nothing is found, or when the call fails -- in
        the failure case the attachment's ``status`` is ``"failed"``
        with a ``reason``, otherwise ``"scored"`` whether or not a
        candidate was found (finding nothing is a successful scan,
        not an error).
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    joined = "\n\n".join(text.strip() for text in input_texts if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip())
    if not joined:
        return None, _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="no input text to scan",
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        signal = judge_detect_protected_attribute_signal(joined, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return None, _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason=f"detector call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored", client, PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply
    )
    return signal, attachment

def run_tool_call_accuracy_check(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    record: dict[str, Any],
    extract_tool_calls: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]] | None],
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Score one record's tool-call accuracy deterministically: no LLM.

    Compares the actual tool calls (extracted from the raw dump)
    against a declared, structured ``gold_tool_calls`` list on the
    sealed record: precision/recall F1 over ``{tool, args}`` pairs,
    the same multiset-overlap idiom ``aixeval.scorecard.f1`` uses
    for text tokens. Reproducible: the same input always gives the
    same score. No tool calls actually made is a legitimate outcome to
    compare, not a failure: it scores 1.0 against an empty gold list
    and 0.0 against a non-empty one, the same as any other multiset
    mismatch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        The original dump, already loaded from JSON, not the sealed
        record. The actual tool calls live here.
    record
        The sealed record; ``gold_tool_calls`` is read from it. Never
        mutated.
    extract_tool_calls
        Which tool-call extractor to use for this dump's shape, e.g.
        ``extract_tool_calls_langfuse``. The caller picks it
        explicitly; no auto-detection, same discipline as ingest.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``tool_call_accuracy_judge`` set,
        the field name both this and ``run_tool_call_accuracy_judge``
        share, see ``aixeval.scorecard.tool_call_accuracy``. On
        failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``) and ``timestamp``,
        no ``model``/``prompt_version``/``raw_reply``, since no LLM is
        called; ``reason`` when failed; ``evidence`` (the specific
        missing/extra calls behind the score, not just the bare F1
        number) when scored with a non-perfect match: unlike an LLM
        judge's rationale, this is exact, not a summary: the full
        mismatch, recoverable from the F1 computation itself rather
        than asked of a model.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    gold_calls = record.get("gold_tool_calls")
    if not isinstance(gold_calls, list):
        return dict(record), _deterministic_attachment(
            "failed", timestamp, reason="record has no gold_tool_calls to compare against"
        )

    actual_calls = extract_tool_calls(payload) or []
    score = _tool_call_f1(actual_calls, gold_calls)
    missing, extra = _tool_call_mismatches(actual_calls, gold_calls)
    new_record = validate_record({**record, "tool_call_accuracy_judge": score})
    return new_record, _deterministic_attachment("scored", timestamp, evidence=_tool_call_evidence(missing, extra))

class ClaudeClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one Claude call. Prompt in, text out. No judge logic."""

    def __init__(self, *, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._client = client if client is not None else anthropic.Anthropic()

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the first text block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user message. No system prompt or judge framing here.
        max_tokens
            Passed straight to the API.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The first text content block in the reply.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
        """
        response = self._client.messages.create(
            model=self._model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        for block in response.content:
            if block.type == "text":
                return block.text
        msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image, return the first text block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user message.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF), base64-encoded
            and sent as an image content block alongside ``prompt``.
        max_tokens
            Passed straight to the API.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The first text content block in the reply.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
        """
        image_block: ImageBlockParam = {
            "type": "image",
            "source": {
                "type": "base64",
                "media_type": guess_mime_type(image_path),
                "data": read_image_base64(image_path),
            },
        }
        text_block: TextBlockParam = {"type": "text", "text": prompt}
        message: MessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [image_block, text_block]}
        response = self._client.messages.create(
            model=self._model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=[message],
        )
        for block in response.content:
            if block.type == "text":
                return block.text
        msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
        raise ValueError(msg)

def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
    """Send one prompt, return the first text block.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prompt
        The full user message. No system prompt or judge framing here.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to the API.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The first text content block in the reply.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
    """
    response = self._client.messages.create(
        model=self._model,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    )
    for block in response.content:
        if block.type == "text":
            return block.text
    msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
    raise ValueError(msg)

def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
    """Send one prompt plus one image, return the first text block.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prompt
        The full user message.
    image_path
        Path to a local image file (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF), base64-encoded
        and sent as an image content block alongside ``prompt``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to the API.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The first text content block in the reply.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no text block (e.g. only a refusal).
    """
    image_block: ImageBlockParam = {
        "type": "image",
        "source": {
            "type": "base64",
            "media_type": guess_mime_type(image_path),
            "data": read_image_base64(image_path),
        },
    }
    text_block: TextBlockParam = {"type": "text", "text": prompt}
    message: MessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [image_block, text_block]}
    response = self._client.messages.create(
        model=self._model,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        messages=[message],
    )
    for block in response.content:
        if block.type == "text":
            return block.text
    msg = f"Claude reply had no text block (stop_reason={response.stop_reason!r})"
    raise ValueError(msg)

def default_model_for(provider: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the model this provider uses when none is given.

def build_client(provider: str, model: str | None = None) -> Provider:
    """Build a judge client for an explicitly chosen provider and model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    provider
        One of ``available_providers()``; case and surrounding spaces
        are ignored.
    model
        The model id to send. ``None`` or blank falls back to
        ``default_model_for(provider)``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``provider`` is not one this toolkit knows, or it has no
        default model (``vllm``) and none was given or set in its env var.
    NotImplementedError
        The named provider is known but has no client wired up
        (defensive only; every declared provider currently is).
    """
    provider = provider.strip().lower()
    if provider not in _MODEL_ENV_VARS:
        known = ", ".join(sorted(_MODEL_ENV_VARS))
        msg = f"Unknown {PROVIDER_ENV_VAR}={provider!r}. Known providers: {known}."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    build = _BUILDERS.get(provider)
    if build is None:
        msg = f"Provider {provider!r} is declared but has no client yet."
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)
    chosen = (model or "").strip() or default_model_for(provider)
    if not chosen:
        model_env_var = _MODEL_ENV_VARS[provider]
        msg = f"Set {model_env_var} to name the model your {provider} server is serving; there is no default."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return build(chosen)

docs.title: cross_modal_hallucination
docs.text:
Cross-modal hallucination verdict: ask a judge model whether output invents content.

Mechanically close to judge_grounding (both are a judge comparing OUTPUT against a source text), but a deliberately separate metric, not a reuse of grounding: this is a Safety-dimension construct ("% claims not in input," lower-is-better), distinct from the Capability-dimension faithfulness grounding measures. The acknowledged overlap is documented here and in aixeval.scorecard.sources, not hidden.

Two mechanisms, both writing the same cross_modal_hallucination_judge field: a declared image_description (text, the original discipline: the judge checks OUTPUT's claims against that text, the same pattern as grounding reading declared evidence text rather than re-deriving it) or a real image_path, sent to a vision- capable Provider.complete_with_image so the judge reads the actual image instead of a text proxy. Exactly one of the two must be passed to judge_cross_modal_hallucination; run_cross_modal_ hallucination_judge prefers image_path when a record has both.

def judge_cross_modal_hallucination(
    output: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    image_description: str | None = None,
    image_path: str | None = None,
    max_tokens: int = 4000,
) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` to grade whether ``output`` hallucinates against the image.

    Exactly one of ``image_description``/``image_path`` must be
    passed. With ``image_description``, the judge reads a declared
    text proxy via ``client.complete``. With ``image_path``, the
    judge reads the real image via ``client.complete_with_image``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output
        What the system under test actually said.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    image_description
        A declared text description of what the image actually shows.
        Mutually exclusive with ``image_path``.
    image_path
        Path to the real image file. Mutually exclusive with
        ``image_description``. Whether the call succeeds depends on
        ``client`` being backed by a vision-capable model; see each
        ``Provider``'s ``complete_with_image`` docstring.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``/``client.complete_with_image``.
        Needs real headroom: a reasoning-capable model can spend most
        of this budget on its own reasoning before ever emitting the
        final ``SCORE:`` line. Default of 4000 matches the value
        confirmed live against the Vector reasoning model
        (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed to fail with
        ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on real traces.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``. Lower is better: 0 is no
        hallucination, 1 is substantially hallucinated.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Neither or both of ``image_description``/``image_path`` were
        passed, or the reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:``
        line.
    """
    if (image_description is None) == (image_path is None):
        msg = "Pass exactly one of image_description or image_path, not both or neither."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if image_path is not None:
        prompt = _IMAGE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(output=output)
        reply = client.complete_with_image(prompt, image_path, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    else:
        prompt = _DESCRIPTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(image_description=image_description, output=output)
        reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return parse_score(reply)

docs.title: evidence
docs.text:
Evidence extraction from a raw dump, not the sealed record.

The generic mechanism is join_evidence_fields: given a flat, human-named dict and a list of field names, join whichever are present. Per-format navigation into that flat shape is the caller's job; only genuinely general, widely-shared formats get a shipped navigator here (Langfuse, a real third-party platform, matching ingest_langfuse). A one-off internal dump shape does not: write a small flattening function for it at the call site and pass the result straight to join_evidence_fields, the same way extract_evidence_langfuse does below.

extract_trajectory_langfuse walks the same observations list but pulls a different shape of information: an ordered trace of steps taken, for judging path quality (see trajectory_optimality), not evidence for judging answer faithfulness (see grounding).

tau-bench's own equivalent, extract_tool_calls_taubench, lives in aixeval.ingest.trace_taubench instead of here: it shares private helpers with that module's parse_taubench_trace, so keeping both in one place avoided a second implementation of the same arguments-shape handling (GPT-4o's JSON-string vs. Sonnet's native dict).

extract_tool_calls_langfuse walks the same list again, filtered to just TOOL-type observations and reshaped as structured {"tool": ..., "args": ...} dicts, for deterministic, no-LLM comparison against a declared gold tool-call list (see tool_call_accuracy), not free text for a judge to read.

def join_evidence_fields(source: dict[str, Any], field_names: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
    """Join whichever named fields are present in ``source``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source
        A flat dict of candidate evidence fields, human-named, not raw
        JSON keys from the original dump.
    field_names
        Which of ``source``'s keys to include, and in what order. A
        future field-picker (UI or LLM-assisted) only ever needs to
        produce this list.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The joined text, or ``None`` if none of ``field_names`` were
        present with usable content.
    """
    texts: list[str] = []
    for name in field_names:
        _append_field_text(texts, source.get(name))
    return "\n\n".join(texts) if texts else None

def extract_trajectory_langfuse(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Pull an ordered, readable trace of the steps a Langfuse-shaped run took.

    Walks the same ``observations`` list ``extract_evidence_langfuse``
    reads, but pulls ``type``/``name``/``input``/``output`` per step
    instead of just ``input``: a trace of what happened, not evidence
    for what the answer should say.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        One numbered line per observation, or ``None`` if there were
        none.
    """
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if not isinstance(observations, list):
        return None
    lines: list[str] = []
    for index, item in enumerate(observations, start=1):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        line = _format_step(index, item)
        if line is not None:
            lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines) if lines else None

def extract_tool_calls_langfuse(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Pull the actual tool calls a Langfuse-shaped run made, as structured data.

    Filters the same ``observations`` list ``extract_trajectory_langfuse``
    reads down to ``type == "TOOL"`` entries only, reshaped as
    ``{"tool": <name>, "args": <input>}``, ready to compare against a
    declared ``gold_tool_calls`` list with no LLM involved.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict] | None
        One entry per tool call, in order, or ``None`` if there were
        none. A tool call with no usable ``name`` is skipped; a missing
        ``input`` becomes ``{}``, never ``None``, so downstream
        comparison never has to special-case it.
    """
    observations = payload.get("observations")
    if not isinstance(observations, list):
        return None
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for item in observations:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("type") != "TOOL":
            continue
        name = item.get("name")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            continue
        args = item.get("input")
        calls.append({"tool": name, "args": args if isinstance(args, dict) else {}})
    return calls or None

class GeminiClient:

        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Parameters

def judge_grounding(evidence: str, output: str, client: Provider, *, max_tokens: int = 4000) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` to grade faithfulness of ``output`` to ``evidence`` on ``[0, 1]``.

    Matches the ``GroundingJudge`` shape ``score_grounding`` already
    accepts (``Callable[[str, str], float]``) once ``client`` is bound,
    e.g. ``functools.partial(judge_grounding, client=my_client)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    evidence
        The evidence text the output should be faithful to.
    output
        What the system under test actually said.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``. Needs real headroom: a
        reasoning-capable model can spend most of this budget on its
        own reasoning before ever emitting the final ``SCORE:`` line.
        Default of 4000 matches the value confirmed live against the
        Vector reasoning model (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed
        to fail with ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on real traces.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(evidence=evidence, output=output)
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return parse_score(reply)

def render_steps(spans: list[Span], *, max_field_chars: int = 600) -> str:
    """Render spans as id-tagged lines so a reply can cite them by id."""
    lines = []
    for span in spans:
        header = [f"[{span.id}]", span.kind]
        if span.agent:
            header.append(f"agent={span.agent}")
        if span.source_type and span.source_type.upper() != span.kind.upper():
            header.append(f"type={span.source_type}")
        if span.parent_id:
            header.append(f"parent={span.parent_id}")
        if span.status and span.status != "ok":
            header.append(f"status={span.status}")
        lines.append(" ".join(header))
        for label, text in (("input", span.input), ("output", span.output)):
            if text:
                clipped = text if len(text) <= max_field_chars else text[:max_field_chars] + " [...]"
                lines.append(f"  {label}: {clipped}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def analyze_hard_stops(
    explanation: dict[str, Any],
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    output: str | None,
    spans: list[Span] | None,
    rationale: dict[str, str],
    client: Provider,
    max_tokens: int = 4000,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Ask ``client`` for a structured incident analysis of the fired hard stops.

    Parameters
    ----------
    explanation
        ``scorecard.hard_stops.explain_hard_stops`` output; must list at least one stop.
    rows
        The graded metric rows the card was built from.
    output
        The run's final output, if any.
    spans
        The run's trace; ``None`` or empty for a simple record.
    rationale
        Earlier judge rationales by metric id, passed through as context.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Headroom for reasoning models, as in the other judges.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``root_cause``, ``responsible_steps``, ``contributing_factors``,
        ``what_would_pass``, ``confidence``, plus ``hard_stops`` (the stops
        analysed), ``prompt_version`` and ``model``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        No hard stop to analyse, or the reply was not valid JSON of the
        required shape, or it cited a step id that is not in the trace.
    """
    stops = [stop["hard_stop"] for stop in explanation.get("hard_stops", [])]
    if not stops:
        msg = "No hard stop fired; nothing to analyse."
        raise ValueError(msg)
    step_list = spans or []
    metrics = [
        {"metric_id": row["metric_id"], "grade": row["grade"], "raw_score": row.get("raw_score")}
        for row in rows
        if row.get("status") == "scored"
    ]
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
        facts=json.dumps(explanation, indent=2, default=str),
        metrics=json.dumps(metrics, indent=2),
        rationales=json.dumps({key: value[:400] for key, value in rationale.items()}, indent=2) if rationale else "{}",
        output=output or "(none)",
        steps=render_steps(step_list) if step_list else "(no trace: this run is a simple record)",
    )
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    analysis = parse_analysis(reply, valid_step_ids={span.id for span in step_list})
    return {**analysis, "hard_stops": stops, "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION, "model": client.model}

Parse and validate an analysis reply. Strict: no guessing.

Source code in src/aixeval/judge/hard_stop_analysis.py 
def parse_analysis(reply: str, *, valid_step_ids: set[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Parse and validate an analysis reply. Strict: no guessing."""
    data = _extract_json(reply)
    root_cause = data.get("root_cause")
    what_would_pass = data.get("what_would_pass")
    steps = data.get("responsible_steps")
    factors = data.get("contributing_factors")
    confidence = data.get("confidence")
    if not isinstance(root_cause, str) or not root_cause.strip():
        raise ValueError("Analysis reply has no root_cause text")
    if not isinstance(what_would_pass, str) or not what_would_pass.strip():
        raise ValueError("Analysis reply has no what_would_pass text")
    if not isinstance(steps, list) or not all(isinstance(step, str) for step in steps):
        raise ValueError("Analysis reply responsible_steps must be a list of step ids")
    if not isinstance(factors, list) or not all(isinstance(factor, str) for factor in factors):
        raise ValueError("Analysis reply contributing_factors must be a list of strings")
    if not isinstance(confidence, int | float) or isinstance(confidence, bool) or not 0.0 <= confidence <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"Analysis reply confidence must be a number in [0, 1], got {confidence!r}")
    normalized = [_normalize_step_id(step) for step in steps]
    unknown = [step for step in normalized if step not in valid_step_ids]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"Analysis reply cites step id(s) not in the trace: {', '.join(unknown)}")
    return {
        "root_cause": root_cause.strip(),
        "responsible_steps": list(dict.fromkeys(normalized)),
        "contributing_factors": [factor.strip() for factor in factors if factor.strip()],
        "what_would_pass": what_would_pass.strip(),
        "confidence": float(confidence),
    }

def extract_live_grounding_evidence(
    payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    spans: list[Span] | None = None,
) -> str | None:
    """Return the evidence text live grounding should judge against.

    Langfuse-shaped dumps use ``extract_evidence_langfuse``, the same
    extractor ``run_grounding_judge`` takes. Other traces fall back to
    span input texts (``collect_trace_input_texts``): what the agent
    saw, not the step log ``format_trajectory`` builds. Trajectory
    text is never used. ``None`` when neither source has usable input.
    """
    if payload is not None and isinstance(payload.get("observations"), list):
        from_dump = extract_evidence_langfuse(payload)
        if from_dump:
            return from_dump
    if spans:
        texts = collect_trace_input_texts(spans)
        return "\n\n".join(texts) if texts else None
    return None
