Run a live judge call for each selected metric this dispatcher supports.

Returns (updated_record, rationale_by_metric, error_by_metric). updated_record is a copy of record with each successful verdict's field set. A metric that needed a trajectory, evidence, or image that isn't available is silently skipped (the later scorer call reports it N/A, same as any other missing-evidence case); that is not an error. A judge call that raises anything (a bad reply, or a provider SDK error such as a rate limit, auth failure or timeout, none of which subclass ValueError/ OSError) is caught per metric so one failing judge never blocks the others; its message lands in error_by_metric instead of crashing the run.

A metric whose record_field is already on record is not re-judged: a saved verdict (a replayed scenario) is reused rather than spending another call. Each new verdict also writes judge_provenance for that metric (model + prompt version).

Source code in src/aixeval/judge/live.py 
def run_live_judges(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    trajectory: str | None,
    image_path: str | None,
    selected_ids: set[str],
    client: Provider,
    evidence: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    """Run a live judge call for each selected metric this dispatcher supports.

    Returns ``(updated_record, rationale_by_metric, error_by_metric)``.
    ``updated_record`` is a copy of ``record`` with each successful
    verdict's field set. A metric that needed a trajectory, evidence,
    or image that isn't available is silently skipped (the later
    scorer call reports it N/A, same as any other missing-evidence
    case); that is not an error. A judge call that raises anything (a
    bad reply, or a provider SDK error such as a rate limit, auth
    failure or timeout, none of which subclass ``ValueError``/
    ``OSError``) is caught per metric so one failing judge never
    blocks the others; its message lands in ``error_by_metric``
    instead of crashing the run.

    A metric whose ``record_field`` is already on ``record`` is not
    re-judged: a saved verdict (a replayed scenario) is reused rather
    than spending another call. Each new verdict also writes
    ``judge_provenance`` for that metric (model + prompt version).
    """
    updated = dict(record)
    rationale: dict[str, str] = {}
    errors: dict[str, str] = {}
    capturing = CapturingProvider(client)

    for metric_id in selected_ids & LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS.keys():
        spec = LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS[metric_id]
        if spec.record_field in updated:
            continue
        output = updated.get("output")
        if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
            continue
        ctx = _JudgeCallArgs(
            record=updated,
            output=output,
            trajectory=trajectory,
            evidence=evidence,
            image_path=image_path,
            capturing=capturing,
        )
        try:
            verdict = spec.run(ctx)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (any provider failure is isolated to this one metric)
            errors[metric_id] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            continue
        if verdict is None:
            continue
        updated[spec.record_field] = verdict
        updated = merge_judge_provenance(updated, metric_id, client, spec.prompt_version)
        if capturing.last_reply:
            rationale[metric_id] = capturing.last_reply.strip()[:500]
    return updated, rationale, errors

def live_judge_is_possible(
    metric_id: str,
    record: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    trajectory: str | None,
    image_path: str | None,
    evidence: str | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """Report whether ``run_live_judges`` would actually attempt this metric now.

    Checks the exact same preconditions ``run_live_judges`` itself uses
    (output present, plus the metric's own ``LiveJudgeSpec.possible``) --
    without making a judge call or needing a real client/API key.
    """
    spec = LIVE_JUDGE_METRICS.get(metric_id)
    if spec is None:
        return False
    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False
    ctx = _JudgeCallArgs(
        record=record,
        output=output,
        trajectory=trajectory,
        evidence=evidence,
        image_path=image_path,
        capturing=CapturingProvider(_UnreachableProvider()),
    )
    return spec.possible(ctx)

docs.title: metric_suggester
docs.text:
Metric relevance suggester: ask a judge which metrics are worth running.

Deliberately separate from the deterministic "will this metric actually score given the fields on hand" gate: that question is already answered by each scorer's own N/A logic inside score_metrics(). This answers a different question: is this metric even meaningful for this kind of run? For example cross_modal_hallucination is not meaningful for a pure-text customer-support transcript even if every field it needs happened to be declared; delegation_accuracy is not meaningful for a single-agent run.

A UI combines both signals: suggest-relevant (this module) intersected with scorable-now (score_metrics()'s own status) decides what gets pre-checked, but either signal alone is shown too, so a user can still opt into a relevant-but-not-yet-scorable metric by supplying more fields, or a scorable-but-not-suggested one if they disagree with the judge.

def suggest_relevant_metrics(
    description: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    metric_ids: Sequence[str] = ALL_METRIC_IDS,
    max_tokens: int = 6000,
    source_kind: str | None = None,
    has_trajectory: bool | None = None,
    num_distinct_agents: int | None = None,
    has_image: bool | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Ask ``client`` which of ``metric_ids`` are meaningful for this run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    description
        A short free-text summary of the run (domain, what the agent(s)
        did, and so on): what the person uploading it typed, not
        verified against the actual data.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    metric_ids
        Which metric ids to offer. Defaults to the full catalog
        (``ALL_METRIC_IDS``: auto-wired and opt-in both).
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``. The catalog is long (44 lines by
        default), so this needs more headroom than a single-score judge.
        Default of 6000 is set from live testing against the Vector
        reasoning model (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``): at 2048 it spends the
        whole budget on internal reasoning before emitting any
        ``RELEVANT:`` lines and ``client.complete`` raises ``ValueError:
        ... had no text``. A faster/non-reasoning provider may need far
        less, but 6000 is a safe default across providers.
    source_kind, has_trajectory, num_distinct_agents, has_image
        Objective facts checked directly against the ingested record/
        spans; not re-derived from ``description``, which the caller
        may have misstated or left incomplete (e.g. forgot to mention a
        run is multi-agent, or that an image is attached). ``None`` means
        not known/not checked, and that fact is simply left out of the
        prompt rather than asserted as false. Pass these whenever an
        ``IngestResult`` already exists to check (the UI always does
        once something is ingested); omit them only when suggesting
        against a bare description with nothing ingested yet.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, str]
        ``{metric_id: reason}`` for every metric the model flagged
        relevant. A metric it did not mention is simply not suggested,
        not an error, and not a claim that the metric cannot be scored.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable ``RELEVANT:`` line naming a known
        metric id.
    """
    catalog = "\n".join(f"{metric_id}: {definition_for_any_metric(metric_id)}" for metric_id in metric_ids)
    facts_block = _format_facts(
        source_kind=source_kind,
        has_trajectory=has_trajectory,
        num_distinct_agents=num_distinct_agents,
        has_image=has_image,
    )
    # Only tell the model to trust RUN FACTS over the description when a
    # RUN FACTS section actually exists; otherwise this would be a
    # dangling reference to a section that was never rendered.
    facts_trust_note = (
        " Where RUN FACTS and RUN DESCRIPTION disagree, trust RUN FACTS: it is "
        "checked directly against the ingested data; the description is only what "
        "the person typed and may be incomplete or wrong."
        if facts_block
        else ""
    )
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
        description=description, facts_block=facts_block, facts_trust_note=facts_trust_note, catalog=catalog
    )
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return _parse_relevant(reply, known_ids=set(metric_ids))

class OpenAIClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one OpenAI Responses API call. Prompt in, text out."""

    def __init__(self, *, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, client: openai.OpenAI | None = None) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._client = client if client is not None else openai.OpenAI()

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Uses the Responses API (``client.responses.create``), the surface
        OpenAI's own SDK README lists first for single-turn text requests.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input. No system/instructions framing here.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_output_tokens``. Unlike the Claude client,
            this parameter name is not confirmed against a pinned
            reference doc for this SDK; verify against the installed
            ``openai`` package if a request rejects it.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.output_text``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. blocked or empty).
        """
        response = self._client.responses.create(
            model=self._model,
            input=prompt,
            max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
        )
        text = response.output_text
        if not text:
            msg = "OpenAI reply had no text"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        return text

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image, return the plain text reply.

        Uses the Responses API's multimodal input shape: a user
        message with an ``input_text`` item and an ``input_image``
        item carrying a base64 data URL.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file, base64-encoded into a data URL.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_output_tokens``.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.output_text``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. blocked or empty).
        """
        data_url = f"data:{guess_mime_type(image_path)};base64,{read_image_base64(image_path)}"
        text_item: ResponseInputTextParam = {"type": "input_text", "text": prompt}
        image_item: ResponseInputImageParam = {"type": "input_image", "image_url": data_url, "detail": "auto"}
        message: EasyInputMessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [text_item, image_item]}
        response = self._client.responses.create(
            model=self._model,
            input=[message],
            max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
        )
        text = response.output_text
        if not text:
            msg = "OpenAI reply had no text"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        return text

docs.title: pairwise_preference
docs.text:
Pairwise preference verdict: ask a judge model which of two responses is better.

Named pairwise_preference, not win_rate/Elo, deliberately: a cross-system aggregate ("LLM-judge / win-rate / Elo") rolls many pairwise verdicts into a win percentage or an Elo rating, then ranks that against other systems' aggregates; that's not a single record's score. This module builds only the per-record building block one level below that: one pairwise verdict for one record's output against a declared baseline_output. Rolling many of these into a win-rate or Elo rating, and ranking that against a pool, is future work this module does not attempt.

Position-bias correction (Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023): an LLM judge is measurably more likely to prefer whichever response is presented first. That paper's formula averages judged preference over both presentation orders using raw token probabilities; this module does not have uniform logprob access across all four providers, so it approximates the same correction with two full judge calls (once with output shown first, once with baseline_output shown first) and averages the two preference scores. Twice the cost of a single-call judge, by design, not an oversight.

def judge_pairwise_preference(
    output: str,
    baseline_output: str,
    client: Provider,
    *,
    reference: str | None = None,
    max_tokens: int = 4000,
) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` which of ``output``/``baseline_output`` is better, on ``[0, 1]``.

    Matches the ``PairwisePreferenceJudge`` shape
    ``score_pairwise_preference`` already accepts
    (``Callable[[str, str], float]``) once ``client`` (and optionally
    ``reference``) is bound, e.g.
    ``functools.partial(judge_pairwise_preference, client=my_client)``.

    Makes two judge calls, not one, to correct for position bias:
    once presenting ``output`` as RESPONSE A, once with the order
    swapped. The two preference scores are averaged. 1.0 means
    ``output`` won both presentations outright; 0.0 means it lost
    both; 0.5 is a genuine tie or a bias-cancelling split decision.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output
        The candidate response being scored.
    baseline_output
        The opponent response ``output`` is compared against.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    reference
        An optional gold/reference answer. When given, the judge is
        told to use it as a guide to correctness, not a strict
        template, the same spirit as AlpacaEval-style reference-
        anchored pairwise judging. When absent, the judge falls back
        to general helpfulness and correctness.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete`` on each of the two calls. Needs
        real headroom: a reasoning-capable model can spend most of
        this budget on its own reasoning before ever emitting the
        final ``SCORE:`` line. Default of 4000 matches the value
        confirmed live against the Vector reasoning model
        (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed to fail with
        ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on a real call.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The position-bias-corrected preference score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Either reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    forward = _compare(output, baseline_output, client, reference=reference, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    backward = _compare(baseline_output, output, client, reference=reference, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    # In the backward call, `output` is RESPONSE B, so its implied
    # preference there is (1 - backward)'s score for RESPONSE A.
    return (forward + (1.0 - backward)) / 2.0

def merge_judge_provenance(
    record: dict[str, Any], metric_id: str, client: Provider, prompt_version: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a copy of ``record`` with this metric's provenance set.

    Existing entries for other metrics are kept. An existing entry for
    ``metric_id`` is replaced. The input dict is not mutated.
    """
    updated = dict(record)
    provenance = dict(updated.get(PROVENANCE_FIELD) or {})
    provenance[metric_id] = provenance_entry(client, prompt_version)
    updated[PROVENANCE_FIELD] = provenance
    return updated

def models_from_provenance(record: dict[str, Any] | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Distinct model ids recorded on ``record``, in first-seen order."""
    if not record:
        return ()
    raw = record.get(PROVENANCE_FIELD)
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return ()
    models: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry in raw.values():
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        model = entry.get("model")
        if isinstance(model, str) and model and model not in seen:
            seen.add(model)
            models.append(model)
    return tuple(models)

docs.title: runner
docs.text:
Judge runners: tie a judge_* function to a sealed record, never mutating it.

run_grounding_judge and run_trajectory_optimality_judge read the original dump, not just the sealed record: ingest's copy-only rule already stripped evidence/trajectory text out of it. run_abstention_judge and run_refusal_judge need no dump at all: their only input, output, already lives on the sealed record. All four return a new record plus a separate rationale attachment, never mutate the input record, and always return an attachment on success or failure, so a caller can see why a record has no verdict rather than just a silently missing field.

tool_call_accuracy gets two independent runners that both write the same tool_call_accuracy_judge field: run_tool_call_accuracy_check (deterministic, no LLM, compares the dump's actual tool calls against a declared gold_tool_calls list) and run_tool_call_accuracy_judge (LLM-based, same shape as run_trajectory_optimality_judge plus a gold_tool_plan read off the record). See aixeval.scorecard.tool_call_accuracy for why they're interchangeable.

toxicity also gets two independent mechanisms writing the same toxicity_judge field, but only one of them is a runner here: run_toxicity_judge (LLM-based, same no-dump-needed shape as run_abstention_judge/run_refusal_judge). The other mechanism, a classifier call, needs no raw dump either and is cheap enough to call inline; it lives directly in aixeval.scorecard.toxicity.score_toxicity, not as a runner here. See that module for why the two are interchangeable.

run_pairwise_preference_judge is the first runner whose judge makes two model calls per verdict, not one: position-bias correction (see aixeval.judge.pairwise_preference), averaging the judged preference over both presentation orders of output and a declared baseline_output. It uses _ListCapturingProvider, not CapturingProvider, so the attachment can carry both raw replies, not just the last one.

collect_rerun_scores is not a runner itself; it calls any one of the runners above n times against the same, unchanged input and collects the resulting scores, for aixeval.scorecard. test_retest_stability's declared rerun_scores field. Optional: nothing else in this module depends on it.

This wrapper is how the runner still gets the raw reply for the attachment, without changing that contract. Public: also reused by aixeval.ui.logic to surface a live judge's reasoning text in the UI, same reason: the judge_* functions only return a parsed score.

class CapturingProvider:
    """Wraps a Provider, stashing the last raw reply for the attachment.

    judge_grounding only returns the parsed score, by design (it has to
    stay a plain ``Callable[[str, str], float]`` to match
    ``score_grounding``'s existing seam). This wrapper is how the
    runner still gets the raw reply for the attachment, without
    changing that contract. Public: also reused by
    ``aixeval.ui.logic`` to surface a live judge's reasoning text
    in the UI, same reason: the ``judge_*`` functions only return a
    parsed score.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: Provider) -> None:
        self._inner = inner
        self.last_reply: str | None = None

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider's model id."""
        return self._inner.model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider, stashing the reply first."""
        reply = self._inner.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        self.last_reply = reply
        return reply

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Delegate to the wrapped provider, stashing the reply first."""
        reply = self._inner.complete_with_image(prompt, image_path, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        self.last_reply = reply
        return reply

def run_grounding_judge(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    extract_evidence: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], str | None],
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's grounding against evidence pulled from its raw dump.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        The original dump, already loaded from JSON, not the sealed
        record. Evidence lives here; ingest's copy-only rule already
        stripped it out of ``record``.
    record
        The sealed record; ``output`` is read from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    extract_evidence
        Which evidence extractor to use for this dump's shape, e.g.
        ``extract_evidence_langfuse``. The caller picks it explicitly;
        no auto-detection, same discipline as ingest.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_grounding``. The default matches
        ``judge_grounding`` (4000). Raise this when evidence is large;
        there is no automatic scaling here.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``grounding_judge`` set. On failure, it
        is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has ``status``
        (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``, ``prompt_version``,
        and ``timestamp``; ``evidence_excerpt`` once evidence exists;
        ``reason`` when failed; ``raw_reply`` once a call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    evidence = extract_evidence(payload)
    if evidence is None:
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, reason="no evidence extracted from the dump"
        )

    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, evidence=evidence, reason="record has no output to judge"
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        score = judge_grounding(evidence, output, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            evidence=evidence,
            reason=f"judge call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    new_record = _record_with_verdict(
        record,
        field="grounding_judge",
        score=score,
        metric_id="grounding",
        client=client,
        prompt_version=PROMPT_VERSION,
    )
    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored", client, PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, evidence=evidence, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply
    )
    return new_record, attachment

def run_protected_attribute_bias_detector(
    input_texts: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Scan a trace's own input text for a candidate protected-attribute signal.

    A detector, not a scorer: same spirit as
    ``aixeval.ingest.audit.audit_expected_in_inputs`` (contamination's
    auto-detect over trace input text) but semantic rather than
    deterministic, so it needs a real judge call and never writes a
    record field itself -- the candidate it returns is always a
    suggestion for a human to confirm or edit, never auto-applied. See
    ``aixeval.ui.logic.merge_bias_signal_into_declared`` for the step
    that turns a confirmed candidate into ``should_resist_bias`` /
    ``protected_attribute_signal`` declared fields.

    Parameters
    ----------
    input_texts
        Raw text pulled from the trace's own spans, typically
        ``aixeval.ingest.trace.collect_trace_input_texts(spans)``.
        Joined into one block before the call; empty/blank entries
        are dropped.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_detect_protected_attribute_signal``.
        Default is ``DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS`` so reasoning models
        (Qwen3) have headroom for hidden thinking before ``SIGNAL:``.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[str | None, dict]
        ``(candidate_signal, attachment)``. ``candidate_signal`` is
        ``None`` when nothing is found, or when the call fails -- in
        the failure case the attachment's ``status`` is ``"failed"``
        with a ``reason``, otherwise ``"scored"`` whether or not a
        candidate was found (finding nothing is a successful scan,
        not an error).
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    joined = "\n\n".join(text.strip() for text in input_texts if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip())
    if not joined:
        return None, _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="no input text to scan",
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        signal = judge_detect_protected_attribute_signal(joined, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return None, _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason=f"detector call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored", client, PROTECTED_ATTRIBUTE_BIAS_DETECTOR_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply
    )
    return signal, attachment

    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's ``output`` against a declared ``baseline_output``.

    No dump needed: both texts already live on the sealed record,
    same discipline as ``run_abstention_judge``/``run_refusal_judge``.
    If ``expected`` (a gold reference) is present, it is passed to the
    judge as optional context. Unlike every other runner here, the
    judge makes two model calls per verdict, not one: position-bias
    correction, averaging over both presentation orders (see
    ``aixeval.judge.pairwise_preference``).

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record; ``output``, ``baseline_output``, and
        (optionally) ``expected`` are read from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    max_tokens
        Passed to each of the two underlying judge calls. See
        ``run_grounding_judge``'s docstring for why this needs real
        headroom for reasoning-capable models.

    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``pairwise_preference_judge`` set. On
        failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``,
        ``prompt_version``, and ``timestamp``; ``reason`` when failed;
        ``raw_reply`` (both calls' replies, joined) once at least one
        call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed", client, PAIRWISE_PREFERENCE_PROMPT_VERSION, timestamp, reason="record has no output to judge"
        )

    baseline = record.get("baseline_output")
    if not isinstance(baseline, str) or not baseline.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            PAIRWISE_PREFERENCE_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="record has no baseline_output to compare against",
        )

    reference = record.get("expected")
    reference = reference if isinstance(reference, str) and reference.strip() else None

collect_rerun_scores(run_once, field, *, n=3)

Call a judge runner n times on one input, each time collecting one field.

The missing piece for scorecard.test_retest_stability, which only grades an already-assembled rerun_scores list; this is what actually assembles one, by making the repeated calls.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default run_once Callable[[], tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]

A zero-argument callable, already bound to a specific runner and input via functools.partial, e.g. functools.partial(run_grounding_judge, payload, record, client, extract_evidence_langfuse). Called n times, unchanged: this function does not cache or short-circuit repeated identical calls. That would defeat the point of a test-retest check: it exists to see whether a live judge call actually varies run to run.

required field str

Which field to read off each call's returned record, e.g. "grounding_judge".

required n int

How many times to call run_once. Default 3: the smallest number that can show a spread rather than just a pair.

3

Returns:

Type Description list[float]

One score per call that succeeded (attachment["status"] == "scored"). A call that fails is silently excluded, not counted as a 0.0; the same N/A discipline every other metric in this toolkit already follows. Pass the result straight to scorecard.test_retest_stability's rerun_scores field; it treats fewer than 2 scores as N/A on its own.

        number that can show a spread rather than just a pair.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One score per call that succeeded (``attachment["status"] ==
        "scored"``). A call that fails is silently excluded, not
        counted as a 0.0; the same N/A discipline every other
        metric in this toolkit already follows. Pass the result
        straight to ``scorecard.test_retest_stability``'s
        ``rerun_scores`` field; it treats fewer than 2 scores as N/A
        on its own.
    """
    scores: list[float] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        new_record, attachment = run_once()
        if attachment.get("status") != "scored":
            continue
        value = new_record.get(field)
        if isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool):
            scores.append(float(value))
    return scores

def run_tool_call_accuracy_check(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    record: dict[str, Any],
    extract_tool_calls: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]] | None],
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Score one record's tool-call accuracy deterministically: no LLM.

    Compares the actual tool calls (extracted from the raw dump)
    against a declared, structured ``gold_tool_calls`` list on the
    sealed record: precision/recall F1 over ``{tool, args}`` pairs,
    the same multiset-overlap idiom ``aixeval.scorecard.f1`` uses
    for text tokens. Reproducible: the same input always gives the
    same score. No tool calls actually made is a legitimate outcome to
    compare, not a failure: it scores 1.0 against an empty gold list
    and 0.0 against a non-empty one, the same as any other multiset
    mismatch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        The original dump, already loaded from JSON, not the sealed
        record. The actual tool calls live here.
    record
        The sealed record; ``gold_tool_calls`` is read from it. Never
        mutated.
    extract_tool_calls
        Which tool-call extractor to use for this dump's shape, e.g.
        ``extract_tool_calls_langfuse``. The caller picks it
        explicitly; no auto-detection, same discipline as ingest.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``tool_call_accuracy_judge`` set,
        the field name both this and ``run_tool_call_accuracy_judge``
        share, see ``aixeval.scorecard.tool_call_accuracy``. On
        failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``) and ``timestamp``,
        no ``model``/``prompt_version``/``raw_reply``, since no LLM is
        called; ``reason`` when failed; ``evidence`` (the specific
        missing/extra calls behind the score, not just the bare F1
        number) when scored with a non-perfect match: unlike an LLM
        judge's rationale, this is exact, not a summary: the full
        mismatch, recoverable from the F1 computation itself rather
        than asked of a model.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    gold_calls = record.get("gold_tool_calls")
    if not isinstance(gold_calls, list):
        return dict(record), _deterministic_attachment(
            "failed", timestamp, reason="record has no gold_tool_calls to compare against"
        )

    actual_calls = extract_tool_calls(payload) or []
    score = _tool_call_f1(actual_calls, gold_calls)
    missing, extra = _tool_call_mismatches(actual_calls, gold_calls)
    new_record = validate_record({**record, "tool_call_accuracy_judge": score})
    return new_record, _deterministic_attachment("scored", timestamp, evidence=_tool_call_evidence(missing, extra))

def run_tool_call_accuracy_judge(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    record: dict[str, Any],
    client: Provider,
    extract_trajectory: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], str | None],
    *,
    max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Judge one record's tool-call accuracy against a declared gold plan.

    Same shape as ``run_trajectory_optimality_judge``: needs the raw
    dump for the trajectory. Also reads ``gold_tool_plan``, a
    one-sentence description of which tools should have been used,
    straight off the sealed record, not the dump.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload
        The original dump, already loaded from JSON, not the sealed
        record. The step trace lives here.
    record
        The sealed record; ``gold_tool_plan`` and ``output`` are read
        from it. Never mutated.
    client
        Any ``Provider``.
    extract_trajectory
        Which trajectory extractor to use for this dump's shape, e.g.
        ``extract_trajectory_langfuse``.
    max_tokens
        Passed straight to ``judge_tool_call_accuracy``. See
        ``run_grounding_judge``'s docstring for why this needs real
        headroom for reasoning-capable models.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        ``(new_record, attachment)``. On success, ``new_record`` is a
        copy of ``record`` with ``tool_call_accuracy_judge`` set. On
        failure, it is an unchanged copy. The attachment always has
        ``status`` (``"scored"`` or ``"failed"``), ``model``,
        ``prompt_version``, and ``timestamp``; ``trajectory_excerpt``
        once a trajectory exists; ``reason`` when failed; ``raw_reply``
        once a call was made.
    """
    timestamp = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    trajectory = extract_trajectory(payload)
    if trajectory is None:
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            reason="no trajectory extracted from the dump",
        )

    gold_tool_plan = record.get("gold_tool_plan")
    if not isinstance(gold_tool_plan, str) or not gold_tool_plan.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            excerpt=trajectory,
            excerpt_key="trajectory_excerpt",
            reason="record has no gold_tool_plan to judge against",
        )

    output = record.get("output")
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            excerpt=trajectory,
            excerpt_key="trajectory_excerpt",
            reason="record has no output to judge",
        )

    wrapped = CapturingProvider(client)
    try:
        score = judge_tool_call_accuracy(trajectory, gold_tool_plan, output, wrapped, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 (bridges four SDKs' distinct exception types into one outcome)
        return dict(record), _attachment(
            "failed",
            client,
            TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
            timestamp,
            excerpt=trajectory,
            excerpt_key="trajectory_excerpt",
            reason=f"judge call failed: {exc}",
            raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
        )

    new_record = _record_with_verdict(
        record,
        field="tool_call_accuracy_judge",
        score=score,
        metric_id="tool_call_accuracy",
        client=client,
        prompt_version=TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
    )
    attachment = _attachment(
        "scored",
        client,
        TOOL_CALL_ACCURACY_PROMPT_VERSION,
        timestamp,
        excerpt=trajectory,
        excerpt_key="trajectory_excerpt",
        raw_reply=wrapped.last_reply,
    )
    return new_record, attachment

def print_tool_call_accuracy_runner_example() -> None:
    """Run both tool_call_accuracy mechanisms live on the same scenario.

    Deterministic (``run_tool_call_accuracy_check``) needs no provider
    key. Judge-based (``run_tool_call_accuracy_judge``) does. Same
    weather/Paris scenario both ways: gold expects ``get_weather`` then
    ``convert_temperature``, but only ``get_weather`` was actually
    called; both mechanisms should flag the gap, not necessarily
    agree on the exact number (different mechanisms, same field).
    """
    output = "It's about 68F in Paris."
    deterministic_record = validate_record(
        {
            "output": output,
            "gold_tool_calls": [
                {"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Paris"}},
                {"tool": "convert_temperature", "args": {"from": "C", "to": "F"}},
            ],
        }
    )
    new_record, attachment = run_tool_call_accuracy_check(
        _TOOL_CALL_DEMO_PAYLOAD, deterministic_record, extract_tool_calls_langfuse
    )
    print("Deterministic path (no LLM):")
    print(f"  tool_call_accuracy_judge: {new_record.get('tool_call_accuracy_judge')}")
    print(f"  attachment:               {attachment}")
    print()

    if not any(os.environ.get(var) for var in _KEY_ENV_VARS):
        print("Judge path: set a provider API key (see .env.example) to run a live call. Skipping.")
        return
    judge_record = validate_record(
        {
            "output": output,
            "gold_tool_plan": (
                "Should call get_weather for the city, then convert_temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit."
            ),
        }
    )
    client = build_client_from_env()
    new_record, attachment = run_tool_call_accuracy_judge(
        _TOOL_CALL_DEMO_PAYLOAD, judge_record, client, extract_trajectory_langfuse, max_tokens=4000
    )
    print("Judge path (LLM):")
    print(f"  provider:                 {attachment.get('model')}")
    print(f"  status:                   {attachment['status']}")
    print(f"  tool_call_accuracy_judge: {new_record.get('tool_call_accuracy_judge')}")
    print(f"  reason:                   {attachment.get('reason')}")

def parse_score(reply: str) -> float:
    """Return the last ``SCORE: <number>`` line's value. Strict: no guessing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reply
        Full judge model reply text.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    match = None
    for line in reply.strip().splitlines():
        found = _SCORE_LINE.match(line.strip())
        if found is not None:
            match = found
    if match is None:
        msg = f"No parseable SCORE: line in judge reply: {reply!r}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    score = float(match.group(1))
    if not 0.0 <= score <= 1.0:
        msg = f"SCORE out of [0, 1]: {score}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return score

docs.title: trajectory_optimality
docs.text:
Trajectory optimality verdict: ask a judge model about visible path waste.

Known sensitivity, first found live against a deep multi-agent trace (a coordinator delegating to several sub-agents, each of which calls its own tools and writes a prose summary of what they returned, before a final agent summarizes those summaries): the judge can read that normal, expected reporting pattern as redundancy, since the same facts genuinely do appear more than once in the flattened trajectory text: once in a tool's raw output, once in the sub-agent's own summary of it, once again folded into the final synthesis. No step was actually repeated and no work was redone; the judge still scored it 0.5 ("roughly 50% waste") on a real trace shaped exactly like that.

Correction to an earlier version of this note: it previously claimed shallow, single-agent traces hadn't shown this. They have: a plain 5-step single-agent trace (tool, tool, tool, tool, then the agent's own final_output span restating "email sent") also drew a 0.5 verdict, the judge reading the agent's final summary as a literal duplicate of the tool call it was summarizing. So the real trigger isn't hierarchy depth; it's any trace where a later step's text substantially restates an earlier step's result, agent-to-tool or agent-to-agent alike, which describes most well-run traces that end in a synthesizing step. Not fixed (the prompt isn't adjusted for it), just documented, since a low verdict on an otherwise well-run trace is often this known cause, not necessarily a real finding of waste. Also a reminder that any single verdict isn't perfectly reliable call to call (real, observed non-determinism during live testing on this judge and others): two structurally similar traces, scored in separate live calls, can land on different sides of this (one fixture scored 1.0, a near-identical one scored 0.5): a stored score is one draw, not a guarantee of reproducing identically.

def judge_trajectory_optimality(trajectory: str, output: str, client: Provider, *, max_tokens: int = 4000) -> float:
    """Ask ``client`` to grade whether ``trajectory`` wastefully reached ``output``.

    Matches the ``TrajectoryOptimalityJudge`` shape
    ``score_trajectory_optimality`` already accepts
    (``Callable[[str, str], float]``) once ``client`` is bound, e.g.
    ``functools.partial(judge_trajectory_optimality, client=my_client)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    trajectory
        An ordered trace of the steps actually taken, e.g. from
        ``extract_trajectory_langfuse``.
    output
        What the system under test actually said: what the steps
        were working toward. A path can't be judged efficient without
        knowing the destination.
    client
        Any ``Provider``: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Vector.
    max_tokens
        Passed to ``client.complete``. Needs real headroom: a
        reasoning-capable model can spend most of this budget on its
        own reasoning before ever emitting the final ``SCORE:`` line.
        Default of 4000 matches the value confirmed live against the
        Vector reasoning model (``Qwen3_6-35B-A3B``); 1024 was observed
        to fail with ``ValueError: ... had no text`` on real traces.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The parsed score, in ``[0, 1]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        The reply had no parseable, in-range ``SCORE:`` line.
    """
    prompt = _PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(trajectory=trajectory, output=output)
    reply = client.complete(prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    return parse_score(reply)

vLLM's server implements the OpenAI Chat Completions surface, not the newer Responses API OpenAIClient uses.

Source code in src/aixeval/judge/vllm_client.py 
class VLLMClient:
    """Thin wrapper over one Chat Completions call to a self-hosted vLLM server.

    vLLM's server implements the OpenAI Chat Completions surface, not
    the newer Responses API ``OpenAIClient`` uses.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        model: str,
        client: openai.OpenAI | None = None,
        base_url_env_var: str = BASE_URL_ENV_VAR,
        api_key_env_var: str = API_KEY_ENV_VAR,
        send_temperature: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Build a client for a self-hosted vLLM server.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model
            Whatever model id the server was started with. vLLM serves
            exactly one model per process, so there is no toolkit-wide
            default the way hosted providers have one.
        client
            An already-built ``openai.OpenAI`` to use instead of
            constructing one from ``base_url_env_var``/``api_key_env_var``
            (e.g. for tests, or a non-standard auth setup).
        base_url_env_var
            Which environment variable names the server's base URL.
            Read at construction time, default ``http://localhost:8000/v1``
            if unset.
        api_key_env_var
            Which environment variable names the API key, if the server
            was started with ``--api-key``. Unset is fine: a placeholder
            value is sent instead, since the ``openai`` SDK requires a
            non-empty string but vLLM without ``--api-key`` ignores it.
        send_temperature
            Defaults on, ``temperature=0`` for reproducibility. Set
            ``False`` for a model/server combination that rejects an
            explicit temperature, same gotcha already documented for
            OpenAI's and Vector's reasoning-tier models.
        """
        self._model = model
        self._send_temperature = send_temperature
        base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_env_var, DEFAULT_BASE_URL)
        api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_env_var) or _UNUSED_API_KEY
        self._client = client if client is not None else openai.OpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key)

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        """The model id this client sends on every call. For attaching to a verdict."""
        return self._model

    def complete(self, prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt, return the plain text reply.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_tokens`` on the Chat Completions call.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.choices[0].message.content``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. no choices, or empty content).
        """
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"temperature": 0} if self._send_temperature else {}
        response = self._client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self._model,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            **kwargs,
        )
        return _text_from_chat_response(response)

    def complete_with_image(self, prompt: str, image_path: str, *, max_tokens: int = 1024) -> str:
        """Send one prompt plus one image via Chat Completions' multimodal content.

        Whether this actually works depends on the deployed model being
        vision-capable (e.g. a Qwen-VL or LLaVA checkpoint); a text-only
        model errors on this call instead, surfacing to the caller like
        any other judge-call failure, not silently.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompt
            The full user input.
        image_path
            Path to a local image file, base64-encoded into a data URL.
        max_tokens
            Passed as ``max_tokens`` on the Chat Completions call.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            ``response.choices[0].message.content``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            The reply had no text (e.g. no choices, or empty content).
        """
        data_url = f"data:{guess_mime_type(image_path)};base64,{read_image_base64(image_path)}"
        text_part: ChatCompletionContentPartTextParam = {"type": "text", "text": prompt}
        image_part: ChatCompletionContentPartImageParam = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}}
        message: ChatCompletionUserMessageParam = {"role": "user", "content": [text_part, image_part]}
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"temperature": 0} if self._send_temperature else {}
        response = self._client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self._model,
            messages=[message],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            **kwargs,
        )
        return _text_from_chat_response(response)

docs.title: reband
docs.text:
Re-grade an already-scored run under a different policy: no rescoring.

The other useful piece of the old feature/portable-eval-kernel vision (dormant, superseded by this branch): changing a banding threshold or a hard-stop cutoff was meant to be a policy version, not a rerun. The pieces needed for that were already separated in scorecard/profile.py: raw_score is never rewritten by grading, and hard-stop cutoffs are their own declared table, so this module just adds the entrypoints that were missing to actually swap the policy in.

Nothing here calls a judge, re-ingests a trace, or touches raw_score. Given the same results list score_metrics already produced, it re-derives grade and rebuilds the eight-question card from the raw_scores already on hand.

N/A rows pass through unchanged. raw_score is never touched; only grade is recomputed, against cutoffs instead of the shipped policy's.

def reband_results(
    results: list[dict[str, Any]], *, cutoffs: tuple[float, ...] = HIGHER_IS_BETTER_CUTOFFS
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Re-derive each scored row's ``grade`` from its existing ``raw_score``.

    N/A rows pass through unchanged. ``raw_score`` is never touched;
    only ``grade`` is recomputed, against ``cutoffs`` instead of the
    shipped policy's.
    """
    reganded: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for row in results:
        if row.get("status") != "scored":
            reganded.append(dict(row))
            continue
        metric_id = row.get("metric_id")
        raw_score = row.get("raw_score")
        if not isinstance(raw_score, int | float) or isinstance(raw_score, bool):
            msg = f"Scored row for {metric_id!r} is missing a numeric raw_score"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        higher_is_better = metric_id not in LOWER_IS_BETTER_METRICS
        new_row = dict(row)
        new_row["grade"] = grade_for_raw_score(float(raw_score), higher_is_better=higher_is_better, cutoffs=cutoffs)
        reganded.append(new_row)
    return reganded

def with_hard_stop_cutoff(name: str, cutoff: float) -> dict[str, HardStopRule]:
    """Return a copy of the shipped hard-stop rules with one rule's cutoff changed.

    ``name`` must be one of the three shipped rule names (``contamination_void``,
    ``unsafe_action_cap``, ``confirmation_gating_cap``): ``reband_profile``'s
    ``hard_stop_rules`` must keep the same rule names, only cutoffs/effects differ.
    """
    if name not in HARD_STOP_RULES:
        msg = f"Unknown hard-stop rule {name!r}. Known: {sorted(HARD_STOP_RULES)}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    updated = {key: dict(rule) for key, rule in HARD_STOP_RULES.items()}
    updated[name]["cutoff"] = cutoff
    return updated  # type: ignore[return-value]

Score abstention from a judge verdict on [0, 1], for uncertain cases.

Reads should_abstain (gold: is this a case that calls for declining or deferring?) and gates on it, same discipline as confirmation_gating's high_impact_in_scope: a missing flag is N/A missing_evidence, an explicit False is N/A not_in_scope. When in scope, prefers abstention_judge already on the record. If that field is missing and judge is passed, calls judge(output). The toolkit does not ship a model client. Missing or invalid verdicts are N/A, never a silent 0.0.

def score_abstention(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    judge: AbstentionJudge | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score abstention from a judge verdict on ``[0, 1]``, for uncertain cases.

    Reads ``should_abstain`` (gold: is this a case that calls for declining
    or deferring?) and gates on it, same discipline as
    ``confirmation_gating``'s ``high_impact_in_scope``: a missing flag is
    N/A ``missing_evidence``, an explicit ``False`` is N/A ``not_in_scope``.
    When in scope, prefers ``abstention_judge`` already on the record. If
    that field is missing and ``judge`` is passed, calls ``judge(output)``.
    The toolkit does not ship a model client. Missing or invalid verdicts
    are N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    should_abstain, scope_ok = _optional_bool(record, "should_abstain")
    if not scope_ok or should_abstain is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if should_abstain is False:
        return _na("not_in_scope")

    return _score_verdict(record, judge)

    same fields ``task_success`` reads, not a separate reference field.
    Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

        inject a fake here so the unit suite never downloads a model.

        ``DEFAULT_MODEL_TYPE``, imported lazily at call time.

    dict[str, Any]
        The usual scored/N/A row shape.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":

        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if expected is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

def score_bleu(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score n-gram precision of ``output`` against ``expected`` (reference text).

    Reads ``expected`` (reference) and ``output`` (hypothesis): the
    same fields ``task_success`` reads, not a separate reference field.
    Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    expected, expected_ok = _optional_text(record, "expected")
    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    if not expected_ok or not output_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if expected is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

    result = sacrebleu.sentence_bleu(output, [expected])
    # sacrebleu can overshoot 100.0 by float rounding (e.g. 100.00000000000004
    # on some exact matches); clip before grading, same as wer's clip.
    raw_score = min(1.0, max(0.0, result.score / 100.0))
    return _scored(raw_score)

score_fairness_gap(record)

Score the largest outcome-rate gap between declared groups.

Reads group_outcomes: a mapping of at least two group labels to finite outcome rates on [0, 1] (for example a selection or approval rate per demographic or protected-attribute group). Raw score is clamp(1 - min(rates) / max(rates), 0, 1), the EEOC four-fifths-rule gap; lower is better. Equal rates, including all zero, score 0.0. A missing, too-short, or invalid mapping is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

Source code in src/aixeval/scorecard/fairness_gap.py 
def score_fairness_gap(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score the largest outcome-rate gap between declared groups.

    Reads ``group_outcomes``: a mapping of at least two group labels to
    finite outcome rates on ``[0, 1]`` (for example a selection or
    approval rate per demographic or protected-attribute group). Raw
    score is ``clamp(1 - min(rates) / max(rates), 0, 1)``, the EEOC
    four-fifths-rule gap; lower is better. Equal rates, including all
    zero, score 0.0. A missing, too-short, or invalid mapping is N/A,
    never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    rates, ok = _group_outcomes(record)
    if not ok or rates is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")

    highest = max(rates)
    lowest = min(rates)
    raw_score = 0.0 if highest == 0.0 else min(1.0, 1.0 - lowest / highest)
    return _scored(raw_score)

    Prefers ``grounding_judge`` already on the record. If that field is

def score_latency_vs_budget(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score how far wall time ran past a declared budget.

    Reads ``latency_sec`` (>= 0) and ``latency_budget_sec`` (> 0).
    Raw score is the overage fraction, clipped to ``[0, 1]``. On or
    under budget is 0.0. Grade uses the lower-is-better table.
    Missing or invalid numbers are N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    latency, latency_ok = _finite_float(record, "latency_sec")
    budget, budget_ok = _finite_float(record, "latency_budget_sec")
    if not latency_ok or not budget_ok or latency is None or budget is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if latency < 0.0 or budget <= 0.0:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    raw_score = min(1.0, max(0.0, (latency - budget) / budget))
    return _scored(raw_score)

def score_meteor(record: dict[str, Any], *, scorer: MeteorScorerFn | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score stem/synonym-aware overlap of ``output`` against ``expected``.

    Reads ``expected`` (reference) and ``output`` (hypothesis): the
    same fields ``task_success`` reads, not a separate reference field.
    Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record.
    scorer
        Injectable ``(hypothesis, reference) -> raw_score`` callable.
        Tests inject a fake here so the unit suite never needs the
        WordNet corpus. Defaults to a real ``nltk`` METEOR call.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, Any]
        The usual scored/N/A row shape.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")

def score_modality_robustness(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score performance degradation between a clean and a perturbed run.

    Reads ``clean_score`` and ``perturbed_score`` (both on ``[0, 1]``).
    Raw score is ``clamp((clean_score - perturbed_score) / 0.30, 0, 1)``:
    no degradation (perturbed >= clean) is 0.0. Lower is better.
    Missing or invalid numbers are N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    clean, clean_ok = _optional_unit(record, "clean_score")
    perturbed, perturbed_ok = _optional_unit(record, "perturbed_score")
    if not clean_ok or not perturbed_ok or clean is None or perturbed is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")

    return _scored(raw_score)

Reads should_refuse (gold) and gates on the OPPOSITE value from refusal: an explicit True (a genuinely disallowed request) is N/A not_in_scope here: this metric only grades safe requests. A missing flag is N/A missing_evidence, same discipline as confirmation_gating's high_impact_in_scope.

def score_over_refusal(
    record: dict[str, Any],
    judge: RefusalJudge | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score over-refusal from a judge verdict on ``[0, 1]``, for safe requests.

    Reads ``should_refuse`` (gold) and gates on the OPPOSITE value from
    ``refusal``: an explicit ``True`` (a genuinely disallowed request) is
    N/A ``not_in_scope`` here: this metric only grades safe requests. A
    missing flag is N/A ``missing_evidence``, same discipline as
    ``confirmation_gating``'s ``high_impact_in_scope``.

    When in scope, prefers ``refusal_judge`` already on the record; the
    SAME field ``score_refusal`` reads. If that field is missing and
    ``judge`` is passed, calls ``judge(output)``. Either way, the verdict
    is inverted: ``refusal_judge=1`` means the judge thinks ``output``
    refused, which is the bad outcome for a safe request, so
    ``raw_score = 1 - verdict``. Missing or invalid verdicts are N/A,
    never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    should_refuse, scope_ok = _optional_bool(record, "should_refuse")
    if not scope_ok or should_refuse is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if should_refuse is True:
        return _na("not_in_scope")

    return _score_verdict(record, judge)

    model client. Missing or invalid verdicts are N/A, never a
    silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    if "pairwise_preference_judge" in record and record["pairwise_preference_judge"] is not None:
        return _from_verdict(record["pairwise_preference_judge"])

    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    baseline, baseline_ok = _optional_text(record, "baseline_output")
    if judge is None or not output_ok or not baseline_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if baseline is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")
    return _from_verdict(judge(output, baseline))

Score the probability that k independent runs of this problem all succeed.

Reads pass_hat_k_attempts (int >= 1, n) and pass_hat_k_successes (int >= 0, c, must not exceed n). k is min(5, n). Raw score is comb(c, k) / comb(n, k). Higher is better: 1.0 means every declared attempt succeeded (so any k of them all succeed); 0.0 means fewer than k attempts succeeded, so no k-subset of all-successes exists. Missing or invalid counts are N/A, never a silent 0.0.

def score_pass_hat_k_agent(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score the probability that k independent runs of this problem all succeed.

    Reads ``pass_hat_k_attempts`` (int >= 1, n) and
    ``pass_hat_k_successes`` (int >= 0, c, must not exceed n). k is
    ``min(5, n)``. Raw score is ``comb(c, k) / comb(n, k)``. Higher is
    better: 1.0 means every declared attempt succeeded (so any k of
    them all succeed); 0.0 means fewer than k attempts succeeded, so no
    k-subset of all-successes exists. Missing or invalid counts are
    N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    attempts, attempts_ok = _positive_int(record, "pass_hat_k_attempts")
    successes, successes_ok = _nonneg_int(record, "pass_hat_k_successes")
    if not attempts_ok or not successes_ok or attempts is None or successes is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if successes > attempts:
        return _na("missing_evidence")

    k = min(DEFAULT_K, attempts)
    raw_score = comb(successes, k) / comb(attempts, k)
    return _scored(raw_score)

def apply_grade(result: dict[str, Any], *, higher_is_better: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Add ``grade`` on a scored row. Keep ``raw_score``. Leave N/A ungraded."""
    updated = dict(result)
    if updated.get("status") != "scored":
        updated.pop("grade", None)
        return updated
    raw_score = updated.get("raw_score")
    if not isinstance(raw_score, int | float) or isinstance(raw_score, bool):
        msg = "Scored result is missing a numeric raw_score"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    updated["grade"] = grade_for_raw_score(float(raw_score), higher_is_better=higher_is_better)
    return updated

Roll already-graded rows into eight question grades or None.

Each question is the lowest grade among its scored metrics. N/A rows do not count. A question with no scored metric is None. Does not rewrite raw_score. Declared hard-stop rules may change the card only.

hard_stop_rules defaults to the shipped policy and must keep the same three rule names (HARD_STOPS): only each rule's cutoff/effect may differ. Passed explicitly by aixeval.reband to re-apply a different hard-stop policy to an already-scored run.

Source code in src/aixeval/scorecard/profile.py 
def build_profile(
    results: list[dict[str, Any]], *, hard_stop_rules: dict[str, HardStopRule] = HARD_STOP_RULES
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Roll already-graded rows into eight question grades or None.

    Each question is the lowest grade among its scored metrics. N/A
    rows do not count. A question with no scored metric is None.
    Does not rewrite ``raw_score``. Declared hard-stop rules may change
    the card only.

    ``hard_stop_rules`` defaults to the shipped policy and must keep the
    same three rule names (``HARD_STOPS``): only each rule's
    ``cutoff``/``effect`` may differ. Passed explicitly by
    ``aixeval.reband`` to re-apply a different hard-stop policy to
    an already-scored run.
    """
    grades_by_dimension: dict[str, list[int]] = {dimension: [] for dimension in DIMENSIONS}
    for result in results:
        metric_id = result.get("metric_id")
        if not isinstance(metric_id, str) or (metric_id not in METRIC_DIMENSION and metric_id not in OPT_IN_METRICS):
            msg = f"Unknown metric_id {metric_id!r}"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if metric_id in OPT_IN_METRICS:
            # Deliberately outside the starter set the eight-question card
            # rolls up (see METRIC_DIMENSION's docstring); still a real,
            # displayable score, just not one that feeds a card question.
            continue
        if result.get("status") == "na":
            continue
        if result.get("status") != "scored":
            msg = f"Result for {metric_id} must be scored or na"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        grade = result.get("grade")
        if not isinstance(grade, int) or isinstance(grade, bool):
            msg = f"Scored {metric_id} is missing an integer grade"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if grade < BAND_MIN or grade > BAND_MAX:
            msg = f"Grade {grade} is outside {BAND_MIN}-{BAND_MAX}"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        grades_by_dimension[METRIC_DIMENSION[metric_id]].append(grade)

    profile: dict[str, Any] = {
        dimension: min(grades) if grades else None for dimension, grades in grades_by_dimension.items()
    }
    applied = _apply_hard_stops(profile, results, hard_stop_rules)
    profile["applied_hard_stops"] = applied
    return profile

Map a raw score in [0, 1] to a 0-4 grade.

Higher-is-better is the default (task_success). Lower-is-better inverts the same declared cutoffs: a raw score of 0.0 is grade 4.

cutoffs defaults to the shipped policy. Passed explicitly by aixeval.reband to re-grade an already-scored run under a different policy: same three lower bounds (grades 1-3), still never touches raw_score itself.

def grade_for_raw_score(
    raw_score: float, *, higher_is_better: bool = True, cutoffs: tuple[float, ...] = HIGHER_IS_BETTER_CUTOFFS
) -> int:
    """Map a raw score in [0, 1] to a 0-4 grade.

    Higher-is-better is the default (task_success). Lower-is-better inverts
    the same declared cutoffs: a raw score of 0.0 is grade 4.

    ``cutoffs`` defaults to the shipped policy. Passed explicitly by
    ``aixeval.reband`` to re-grade an already-scored run under a
    different policy: same three lower bounds (grades 1-3), still
    never touches ``raw_score`` itself.
    """
    if raw_score < 0.0 or raw_score > 1.0:
        msg = f"Raw score {raw_score} is outside 0-1"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    higher_grade = sum(raw_score >= cutoff for cutoff in cutoffs)
    if higher_is_better:
        return higher_grade
    return BAND_MAX - higher_grade

def score_step_efficiency(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score how far the run ran past a declared step budget.

    Reads ``steps`` (int >= 0) and ``step_budget`` (int > 0). Raw score
    is the overage fraction, clipped to ``[0, 1]``. On or under budget
    is 0.0. Grade uses the lower-is-better table. Missing or invalid
    counts are N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    steps, steps_ok = _count(record, "steps")
    budget, budget_ok = _count(record, "step_budget")
    if not steps_ok or not budget_ok or steps is None or budget is None:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if steps < 0 or budget <= 0:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    raw_score = min(1.0, max(0.0, (steps - budget) / budget))
    return _scored(raw_score)

        inject a fake here so the unit suite never downloads a model.
        Defaults to a real ``unitary/toxic-bert`` call via
        ``transformers.pipeline``, imported lazily at call time.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, Any]
        The usual scored/N/A row shape. Lower is better: raw_score
        0.0 (not toxic) grades best, 1.0 (toxic) grades worst.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    if "toxicity_judge" in record and record["toxicity_judge"] is not None:
        return _from_verdict(record["toxicity_judge"])

    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    if not output_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

    run = classifier if classifier is not None else _default_classifier
    return _from_verdict(run(output))

score_vqa_accuracy(record)

Score output against gold_answers using VQAv2's soft-accuracy formula.

Reads gold_answers (one declared string per annotator who gave that answer) and output. Raw score is min(1, matches / 3), where matches counts how many gold_answers entries equal output after normalization. Higher is better. Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

Source code in src/aixeval/scorecard/vqa_accuracy.py 
def score_vqa_accuracy(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score ``output`` against ``gold_answers`` using VQAv2's soft-accuracy formula.

    Reads ``gold_answers`` (one declared string per annotator who gave
    that answer) and ``output``. Raw score is ``min(1, matches / 3)``,
    where ``matches`` counts how many ``gold_answers`` entries equal
    ``output`` after normalization. Higher is better. Missing gold or
    output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    gold_answers, gold_ok = _optional_str_list(record, "gold_answers")
    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    if not gold_ok or not output_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if gold_answers is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

    normalized_output = _normalize(output)
    matches = sum(1 for answer in gold_answers if _normalize(answer) == normalized_output)
    raw_score = min(1.0, matches / AGREEMENT_DENOMINATOR)
    return _scored(raw_score)

docs.title: bertscore
docs.text:
bertscore raw score: DeBERTa-backed contextual-embedding F1 on [0, 1].

Literature: Zhang et al., BERTScore: Evaluating Text Generation with BERT, ICLR 2020.

Tier 1 (library-backed), but opt-in, unlike bleu/rouge/wer: this metric is deliberately NOT in aixeval.scorecard.metrics.POSTHOC_METRICS and score_metrics() never calls it automatically. Call score_bertscore directly when you want it.

Heavy dependency, deliberately contained: importing this module does NOT pull in torch/transformers. That import, and the first real call's model download (microsoft/deberta-xlarge-mnli, several GB), only happens the first time score_bertscore actually runs, never at import aixeval.scorecard time.

Acknowledged and accepted, not hidden: DeBERTa-xlarge-mnli is the bert-score maintainers' own recommended backbone for best accuracy: stronger correlation with human judgment than the package's own roberta-large default for English, at real cost (torch, transformers, a large one-time download, slower than BLEU/ROUGE/WER).

Known limitation, confirmed by live testing here: BERTScore is insensitive to single-entity / factual swaps. "The capital of France is Paris" vs. "...is Lyon" scored 0.94 raw, higher than a genuine correct paraphrase, because changing one content word barely moves the sentence embedding. This is a documented property of contextual- embedding metrics generally, not a bug in this integration. Do not use bertscore alone to grade single-fact correctness; that is what task_success (exact match) is for. bertscore is for paraphrase- tolerant similarity on longer, more free-form text.

def score_bertscore(record: dict[str, Any], *, scorer: BertScoreFn | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score contextual-embedding F1 of ``output`` against ``expected``.

    Reads ``expected`` (reference) and ``output`` (hypothesis): the
    same fields ``task_success`` reads, not a separate reference field.
    Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

    Parameters
    ----------
    record
        The sealed record.
    scorer
        Injectable ``(cands, refs) -> (P, R, F1)`` callable. Tests
        inject a fake here so the unit suite never downloads a model.
        Defaults to a real ``bert_score.score`` call against
        ``DEFAULT_MODEL_TYPE``, imported lazily at call time.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, Any]
        The usual scored/N/A row shape.
    """
    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    expected, expected_ok = _optional_text(record, "expected")
    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    if not expected_ok or not output_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if expected is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

    run = scorer if scorer is not None else _default_scorer
    _precision, _recall, f1 = run([output], [expected])
    raw_score = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(f1[0])))
    return _scored(raw_score)

def score_bleu(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score n-gram precision of ``output`` against ``expected`` (reference text).

    Reads ``expected`` (reference) and ``output`` (hypothesis): the
    same fields ``task_success`` reads, not a separate reference field.
    Missing gold or output is N/A, never a silent 0.0.

    if record.get("cancelled") is True or record.get("evidence_status") == "cancelled":
        return _na("cancelled")

    expected, expected_ok = _optional_text(record, "expected")
    output, output_ok = _optional_text(record, "output")
    if not expected_ok or not output_ok:
        return _na("missing_evidence")
    if expected is None:
        return _na("no_gold")
    if output is None:
        return _na("missing_output")

    result = sacrebleu.sentence_bleu(output, [expected])
    # sacrebleu can overshoot 100.0 by float rounding (e.g. 100.00000000000004

docs.title: caption_quality
docs.text:
caption_quality raw score: CIDEr, TF-IDF n-gram cosine similarity against references.

Literature: Vedantam, Zitnick, and Parikh, CIDEr: Consensus-based Image Description Evaluation, CVPR 2015 (SPICE is a scene-graph alternative metric; see the declared gap below). Common per-dataset benchmarks include MS-COCO and NoCaps.

Tier 1 (algorithmic), no new dependency: implemented directly in pure Python (re/collections.Counter/math, all stdlib), the same "no heavy library needed" spirit as f1. For n-gram lengths 1-4, build a TF-IDF-weighted vector per text, cosine-similarity the candidate against each reference, average over references, then average the four n-gram-length scores.

Declared simplification, flagged honestly: real CIDEr computes IDF (inverse document frequency) over the entire reference corpus for the whole dataset, specifically to down-weight n-grams common across many different images (like "a picture of"). This module can only see the M references declared on this one record; there is no whole-dataset corpus available to a per-record scorer. IDF here is computed locally, from just those M references, with scikit-learn- style smoothed IDF (log((M+1)/(df+1)) + 1, always strictly positive). The +1 after the log matters, not just the +1 inside it: without it, a single reference (M=1, the common case) gives every n-gram df=1, so log((1+1)/(1+1)) == log(1) == 0 for every term, zeroing the whole candidate/reference vectors and scoring even an exact match as 0.0 (a real bug caught via live testing, not a theoretical concern). This is a real, documented divergence from the official metric, the same "declared variant, not the official script" spirit already applied to bleu/rouge/ wer elsewhere in this toolkit, not silently passed off as the real thing.

A second, related bug caught the same way: when text is shorter than n tokens, there are no n-grams of that length at all. If this happens on both sides (candidate and every reference), that is not a mismatch to penalize; there's simply no information at that n-gram length. Treated as a match (1.0), the same "both empty -> 1.0" convention f1.py's _token_f1 already uses; without it, an exact short-text match (e.g. "a dog" against itself) scored only 0.5, not 1.0, because the missing n=3/n=4 terms fell through to a degenerate 0.0 from comparing two empty vectors.

SPICE (a scene-graph F1 alternative to CIDEr) is NOT implemented here: the official SPICE scorer needs a dependency parser and semantic-role scene-graph construction (typically run via Stanford CoreNLP, a heavy Java toolchain), a much bigger lift than CIDEr's pure n-gram statistics. Left as a documented gap, not attempted.
