docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Concepts

How the scorecard works

Dimensions, bands, hard stops, and how to read grades.

These pages describe what the scorecard measures and how to read it. They are aimed at evaluators and tech leads, not only Python contributors.

docs.title: Flow (post-hoc)
docs.text:
1. Ingest: normalize a simple JSON dump or a trace (Langfuse, OTel, Patronus, Inspect AI, and others) into one sealed record per run.
  2. Score: run metrics from the catalog; missing evidence is N/A, not a silent 0.
  3. Card: roll metric grades into eight questions (0–4 each), then apply declared hard stops (contamination, unsafe action, confirmation gating).

The toolkit never rewrites a raw metric score when a hard stop fires; it only caps or voids card questions per policy.

docs.title: Read next
docs.text: Topic Page Dimensions, bands, literature vs policy Methodology What a high grade does not mean Interpreting results Judge variance, fairness N/A, cost Limitations All metric ids and required fields Metric catalog

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Extend

Contribute and customize

Add metrics upstream or run private scorers alongside the card.

The core package ships 47 named metrics and an eight-question card. You can extend it in two ways:

docs.title: Contribute a first-party metric
docs.text:
Add a scorer under src/aixeval/scorecard/, register it in the central catalog tables, and open a pull request. The maintainer checklist lives in Add a metric.

There is no runtime plugin hook today: upstream metrics are wired explicitly in score_metrics(). A registry or entry-point design may come later if third-party catalogs become common.

docs.title: Use a private metric (no upstream merge)
docs.text: Implement a scorer that returns the same result shape as built-in metrics (metric_id, status, raw_score or na_reason, grade when scored). Combine its rows with score_metrics() output before build_profile(), or keep a separate report outside the eight-question card. See Add a metric: private metrics.

docs.title: Contributing code and docs
docs.text: Contributing: style, tests, and review expectations.

docs.title: Add a metric
docs.text: This guide is for first-party metrics merged into aixeval. Follow the steps in order; the test suite enforces that registries stay in sync.

docs.title: Scorer contract
docs.text:
Each metric lives in src/aixeval/scorecard/<metric_id>.py and exposes:

  • A module-level METRIC_ID = "<metric_id>" string (snake_case).
  • score_<metric_id>(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any].

Return shape:

status Fields scored metric_id, raw_score on [0, 1], grade (0–4), band_label na metric_id, na_reason (use require_na_reason from na_reasons.py)

Use apply_grade() from profile.py for scored rows so bands match the rest of the catalog. Missing evidence must be N/A, never a silent 0.0.

Study an existing scorer:

  • Computed / library: bleu.py
  • Token overlap: f1.py
  • Declared bools: see error_recovery.py, unsafe_action.py

Document literature, edge cases, and required record fields in the module docstring. The metric catalog table is a summary; the module is the detailed source until per-metric pages are generated.

docs.title: Registration checklist
docs.text:
Complete every row that applies to your metric.

Step File What to add 1 src/aixeval/scorecard/<metric_id>.py Scorer + tests in tests/test_<metric_id>.py (or named file) 2 src/aixeval/scorecard/metrics.py Id in POSTHOC_METRICS or OPT_IN_METRICS 3 metrics.py METRIC_DIMENSION[<id>]: one of the eight card questions 4 metrics.py Import + call inside score_metrics() (skip if opt-in) 5 definitions.py One sentence in METRIC_DEFINITIONS or OPT_IN_METRIC_DEFINITIONS 6 sources.py Row in METRIC_SOURCES (kind, citation, note) 7 reband.py If lower-is-better, list id in LOWER_IS_BETTER_METRICS 8 profile.py Only if policy needs it: new HARD_STOP_RULES entry (rare) 9 docs/metric-catalog.md Summary row until catalog generation lands (Phase 2) 10 Optional deps pyproject.toml via uv add; document in user guide if heavy

docs.title: POSTHOC vs opt-in
docs.text:
POSTHOC ids run automatically in score_metrics() and appear in default UI flows. Put a metric in OPT_IN when:

  • It needs large downloads or GPU libs (e.g. bertscore, clip_score).
  • Automatic inclusion would distort the card (e.g. meteor on short exact answers: see the comment at the top of metrics.py).

Opt-in metrics still need definitions for ALL_METRIC_IDS and the judge suggester; callers invoke score_<id>(record) directly.

docs.title: Lower-is-better
docs.text: Call apply_grade(..., higher_is_better=False) and add the id to LOWER_IS_BETTER_METRICS. tests/test_reband.py scans scorer source and fails if the set drifts.

docs.title: Hard stops
docs.text: Hard stops (contamination, unsafe action, confirmation gating) only change card questions; they never change raw_score. New metrics almost never add hard stops. If you believe one is required, discuss in the PR and update HARD_STOP_RULES in profile.py plus docs/methodology.md.

docs.title: Tests that guard the catalog
docs.text:
These tests fail when registries drift:

  • tests/test_definitions.py: every POSTHOC_METRICS / opt-in id has a definition
  • tests/test_metric_sources.py: METRIC_SOURCES covers all posthoc ids
  • tests/test_metric_dimensions.py: METRIC_DIMENSION keys match posthoc set
  • tests/test_score_metrics.py: one row per posthoc id
  • tests/test_reband.py: lower-is-better set matches scorer code

Run before review:

uv sync --dev
uv run pytest tests/test_<your_metric>.py tests/test_definitions.py tests/test_metric_sources.py
uv run mypy src
uv run ruff check .

docs.title: Private metrics without upstream merge
docs.text:
You do not have to fork score_metrics() for experiments:

  1. Implement score_my_metric(record) with the same return dict shape.
  2. After ingest, call it alongside score_metrics(record).
  3. Pass the combined list to build_profile() only if you assigned METRIC_DIMENSION-compatible behavior and accept card aggregation rules (each question grade is derived from metrics mapped to that dimension).

Rows with unknown metric_id values are not folded into the card unless you extend profile logic upstream. Keeping a sidecar JSON report is fine for org-only metrics.

docs.title: Pull request
docs.text:
Fill out .github/pull_request_template.md. Link an issue if one exists. See Contributing for style and the full dry-run list.

In the PR description, state:

  • Mechanism (declared / computed / judge / overlay)
  • Required record fields (ingest contract)
  • Why POSTHOC vs opt-in
  • Any new optional dependency and license impact

Unit tests cover scorecard, ingest, judge, and UI logic without live traces. Tests marked integration_test skip when no provider key is in .env; see the user guide. Streamlit AppTests need uv sync --group ui.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• Public docs (docs/): do not use em dashes (Unicode U+2014). Use commas, colons, parentheses, or semicolons instead.
  • Python >=3.12, src/ layout, uv for dependencies
  • PEP 8; NumPy docstrings; types required (ruff + mypy)
  • Line length 120 (ruff)
  • Tests: pytest; mark live-provider tests @pytest.mark.integration_test
  • Prefer uv run so tools use the project environment
